SESAME is the sign-in library for Wayne State's PHP apps. It checks who someone is and hands your app a verified identity. Your app keeps the session. Every driver ends in your app's `findOrImportUser(Identity)`, so moving from CAS to OpenID Connect is an `.env` change.

`$ composer require waynestate/sesame`

**Already included in [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/) and in every [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/) app.** Use SESAME on its own to add sign-in to an app you already have.

[Try a key](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#keys) [Watch one get cut](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/#duplicator)

Service counter. Same door for every key.

The pegboard

### One blank per protocol

Each key on the board is a driver. All six are cut now. SAML is the newest, and it waits on its own hook until an app asks for it: opt-in, with no IdP picked for you. Pick one to see its `.env` line and what it checks. Whichever you pick, the door is the same: your app's `findOrImportUser(Identity)`.

.env

`SESAME_DRIVER=cas`

**cas:** CAS 2.0 by default. The CAS server sends the user back with a ticket; SESAME validates it once, then drops it from the address bar. The door opens.

The duplicator

### Swap the blank. Keep the door.

This is an app moving from `cas` to `gateway`, the move Citadel apps will make once Drawbridge is live. Until then, `cas` is the driver to use on Citadel. Scroll down and the machine copies the cut onto the new key.

A key duplicator copies the cut of a cas key onto a gateway blank. As it cuts, the config line SESAME_DRIVER=gateway is typed under the new key. The new key goes into the same door, the door opens, and ab1234 is in.

1. **Clamp a gateway blank.** It has a new head and no cut yet.
2. **Trace the cut.** The tracer follows the cas key while the cutter copies it onto the blank.
3. **The cut is one config line.** Set `SESAME_DRIVER=gateway`, then add the gateway's public key, issuer, audience and trusted proxies. You don't touch your code.
4. **Open sesame.** Your `findOrImportUser(Identity)` runs as before, and ab1234 is signed in.

Three doorways

### Same lock, any frame

SESAME works in raw PHP, in Laravel with Blade, and in Laravel with Inertia and Vue. The install line is the same for all three. What changes is how you wire it in.

Install Windows, macOS and Linux: the same line

`$ composer require waynestate/sesame`

Job 01

#### Raw PHP

Your app owns the session, so you start it and HELMET sets the cookie flags. Set `session.gc_maxlifetime` to 7200, or PHP signs people out after 24 quiet minutes.

```
session_start();
// build $sesame (see the README), then:
sesame($sesame);
$user = sesame_login();
```

Protected pages call `sesame_user()`. Login and logout end the script after they redirect, so nothing below them runs.

Job 02

#### Laravel + Blade

Laravel finds the service provider by itself. Publish the config, then put `auth.sesame` on the routes that need a signed-in user.

```
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=sesame-config

Route::get('/dashboard', fn () => view('dashboard'))
    ->middleware('auth.sesame');
```

A guest is sent to `sesame.login`. A JSON request from a guest gets a 401.

Job 03

#### Laravel + Inertia/Vue

It's the same Laravel adapter. The middleware runs on the server, so a guest never receives the Vue page.

```
Route::get('/vault', fn () => Inertia::render('Vault'))
    ->middleware(['auth.sesame', 'sesame.mfa']);
```

`sesame.mfa` also checks that the user's last MFA is recent enough: 8 hours unless you set another limit.

#### No PHP on the machine?

Docker runs the tests on PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. Paste the lines as they are into PowerShell, bash or zsh.

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

Work orders

### Have your agent cut it

Five prompts for whatever coding agent you use. Copy one, or open it in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each one names the kind of app it's for and what the agent must leave alone, and every one tells it to ask you before it guesses.

#### Get started with SESAME

Works out what kind of app you have and which driver it needs, then writes a plan. It changes nothing.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent helping a Wayne State University developer add sign-in to the PHP app in this folder with SESAME. SESAME is the auth library of WELD, the Wayne State application stack: it hands the app a verified identity and leaves the session to the app. Every driver (cas, gateway, oauth2, oidc, and fake for local work) ends in the app's findOrImportUser(Identity), and switching driver is a config change.

Read first:
- https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of SESAME's pages, each one as Markdown. Fetch the pages you need; do not work from memory.
- This app's composer.json and composer.lock, its entry scripts or routes, and how it handles users and sessions today.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for sesame, and list_stack_rules for the auth chapter. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt

Task:
1. Say which kind of app this is: raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, or Laravel with Inertia and Vue. If it uses wayne-cas today, say so: SESAME has a shim for that.
2. Pick the driver: cas for browser sign-in against Academica, oidc for Entra sign-in, oauth2 for an API that takes bearer tokens, gateway only behind the auth gateway. Say why.
3. List the settings that driver needs and where each value comes from: the environment, or the Playbook.
4. Write the plan as numbered steps, starting with `composer require waynestate/sesame`. Change nothing yet.

Constraints:
- The app owns the session. SESAME never starts one and never sets a cookie; never ask it to.
- Fail closed: no default user, no fallback login, no bare header trusted as an identity.
- The fake driver is for local work only; it refuses to boot in production.
- Playbook is private on git.wayne.edu. If you get a 404, ask the Enterprise Applications team for read access. SESAME runs without it, from the environment alone.
- Never put a secret, a token or a key in a committed file.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch anything that deploys.

Output: the app kind, the driver and why, a settings table (setting, where it comes from, value or ask), the plan, then your questions.
```

#### Or pick your doorway

#### SESAME in a raw PHP app

Sets up the config, the driver and a user resolver by hand, on your app's own session, with a logout that only accepts a POST.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent adding sign-in with SESAME to a raw PHP app (no framework) at Wayne State University. SESAME is the auth library of WELD, the Wayne State application stack.

Read first:
- https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README's Raw PHP section and the section for the driver this app needs.
- This app's composer.json, its front controller or entry scripts, and where it calls session_start().
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for sesame, and list_stack_rules with permutation raw-php for the auth rules. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.

Task:
1. Install with `composer require waynestate/sesame`.
2. Build Config, the driver from DriverFactory, a UserResolver whose findOrImportUser(Identity) returns this app's user, and NativeSession, as the README shows; then call sesame() once.
3. Sign in with sesame_login(), read the user on protected pages with sesame_user(), and sign out with a POST form that carries sesame_logout_token().
4. Show me each file you would change before you write it.

Constraints:
- Start the session yourself, before SESAME. Set session.gc_maxlifetime to at least SESAME's idle timeout (7200 for the default 120 minutes), or PHP ends sessions after 24 quiet minutes.
- Logout is POST only, with the token. Never make it a GET link.
- Read the CAS base URL and the other settings from the environment, or with Setting::get; never hard-code them.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch anything that deploys.

Output: the changes as a diff per file, then how to try it locally with the fake driver, then your questions.
```

#### SESAME in a Laravel app with Blade

Publishes the config, writes a user resolver, puts auth.sesame on your routes and adds a sign-out form with a CSRF token.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent adding sign-in with SESAME to a Laravel app that renders its pages with Blade, at Wayne State University. SESAME is the auth library of WELD, the Wayne State application stack; its Laravel adapter is a discovered service provider that holds no rules of its own.

Read first:
- https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README's Laravel section and the section for the driver this app needs.
- This app's composer.json, config/, routes/web.php, its User model, .env.example and config/session.php.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for sesame, and list_stack_rules with permutation laravel-blade for the auth rules. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.

Task:
1. Install with `composer require waynestate/sesame` and publish the config with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=sesame-config`.
2. Write the user resolver class and name it in SESAME_USER_RESOLVER. Add every setting the driver needs to .env.example, with no real values.
3. Guard the app's routes with auth.sesame (and sesame.mfa where MFA is required), and give the layout a sign-out form that posts to /logout with @csrf.
4. Show me the whole diff before you write it.

Constraints:
- Keep the adapter's sesame.login route name, even if the app takes the routes over.
- The session store must be shared (database or redis), never local files.
- The cas and oauth2 drivers need a PSR-18 client: Guzzle if the app has it, or a bound client.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch migrations or anything that deploys.

Output: the diff, the .env.example lines, then your questions.
```

#### SESAME in a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue

Uses the same adapter. Routes are guarded on the server, and Vue gets only the user fields it needs as a prop.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent adding sign-in with SESAME to a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue, at Wayne State University. SESAME is the auth library of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. The Laravel adapter guards routes on the server, so a page that needs a signed-in user is never sent to a guest.

Read first:
- https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README's Laravel section and the section for the driver this app needs.
- This app's composer.json, config/, routes/web.php, its User model, .env.example, and the Inertia middleware that shares props (often HandleInertiaRequests).
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for sesame, and list_stack_rules with permutation laravel-inertia-vue for the auth rules. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.

Task:
1. Install with `composer require waynestate/sesame` and publish the config with `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=sesame-config`.
2. Write the user resolver class and name it in SESAME_USER_RESOLVER. Add every setting the driver needs to .env.example, with no real values.
3. Guard the Inertia routes with auth.sesame (and sesame.mfa where MFA is required). Share only the user fields the Vue pages need, never the whole identity.
4. Sign out with a POST to /logout that carries Laravel's CSRF token. Check how this app's Inertia setup sends that token before you rely on it.
5. Show me the whole diff before you write it.

Constraints:
- Authorization lives on the server. A Vue component may hide a button; it never decides who gets in.
- Keep the adapter's sesame.login route name. The session store must be shared (database or redis).
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch migrations, the build, or anything that deploys.

Output: the diff, the .env.example lines, then your questions.
```

#### Move a Laravel app from wayne-cas to SESAME

The shim keeps the old names, so most of the move is the mapping table. The agent lists every wayne-cas part before it swaps one.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent moving a Laravel app at Wayne State University from wayne-cas to SESAME, the auth library of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. SESAME ships a wayne-cas shim that keeps the old names and behavior and logs once that it is a deprecated bridge.

Read first:
- https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the README's Moving from wayne-cas section and its mapping table.
- This app's composer.json, config/wayne-cas.php if there is one, the User model, the routes and middleware that use WayneAuthenticate, and every call to auth()->login().
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for sesame. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.

Task:
1. List every wayne-cas part the app uses, with the file and line, and the SESAME part that replaces it from the mapping table.
2. Plan the move: install with `composer require waynestate/sesame`, set sesame.cas.base_url from wayne-cas.root, make the User model implement WayneCasable with the ReadOnlyAttributes trait, and swap the middleware for the wayne.cas alias.
3. Say whether the app turns use2FA on. The shim does not carry it; it logs a warning and leaves 2FA to the app. Ask me what should replace it.
4. Change nothing yet.

Constraints:
- Keep the model's static findOrImportUser: the shim finds the user the way wayne-cas did.
- Remove wayne-cas only after the app signs in through SESAME, never in the same step.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you touch anything that deploys.

Output: the parts table (wayne-cas part, file and line, SESAME part), the plan as numbered steps, then your questions.
```

The agent reads the same pages you do: [llms.txt](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists them, [llms-full.txt](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds them in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). Nothing here phones home. The buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked.

Posted by the door

### Shop rules

1. **The app owns the session.** SESAME never starts one and never touches a cookie.
2. **A new session ID at login,** before anything is stored in it.
3. **Fail closed.** A non-200 answer from the CAS server, malformed XML or an empty user ends the login. There is no default user to fall back on.
4. **No bare headers.** The gateway driver trusts only a signed assertion that comes through a trusted proxy, and it refuses one it has seen before.
5. **The fake key stays home.** The fake driver refuses to boot in production.
6. **No default locks.** Required settings, like the CAS base URL, have no default. Your app only talks to a server you chose.
7. **MFA fails closed.** If there's no sign-in time or MFA method, or the MFA is too old, the request is denied.
8. **Logout shuts the door.** It takes a POST with a token, then sends `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Clear-Site-Data: "cache", "storage"` so the back button can't show a signed-in page.

[Every practice, with its sources](https://github.com/waynestate/sesame/blob/main/BEST_PRACTICES.md)

#### Hours

- **Idle**: 120 min
- **Absolute**: 720 min
- **MFA good for**: 8 h

SESAME checks both session clocks each time `user()` is called. A stale session finds the door locked.

Cross-reference

### Re-key from wayne-cas

Moving a Laravel app off wayne-cas? SESAME ships a shim that keeps the wayne-cas names and behavior, so this table is most of the work. The shim logs once that it's a deprecated bridge. It doesn't carry `use2FA`, so that part stays with your app.

**wayne-cas names and the SESAME names that replace them**

| Old part (wayne-cas) | Fits (SESAME) |
| --- | --- |
| `wayne-cas.root` | `sesame.cas.base_url` |
| `auth.providers.users.model` | `auth.providers.users.model`, unchanged |
| `WayneCasable` trait | `implements WayneCasable` + `use ReadOnlyAttributes` |
| `WayneAuthenticate` middleware | the `wayne.cas` middleware alias |
| `auth()->login($user)` | `app(Sesame::class)->user()` |
| `use2FA` | not carried; the shim logs a warning once when it's on |

On the key ring

### SESAME in WELD

SESAME is one part of Wayne State's app stack. Here's where it sits in a signed-in request on Citadel, followed by the rest of the stack.

1. [**Drawbridge**](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/) signs the assertion at the edge, once it's live
2. **SESAME** checks it and gives your app an identity
3. [**HELMET**](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/) hardens the session cookie
4. [**WayneUI**](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/) renders the signed-in page

- [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/)Wayne State's design system
- [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/)the written standards
- [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/)checks an app against them
- [Preflight](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/)GitLab CI components
- SESAMEsigns the user in · you are here
- [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/)headers and hardening
- [Pinstripe](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/)code style presets
- [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/)starts an app in any of the five shapes
- [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/)Laravel and Vue, stack installed
- [Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/)the Citadel sign-in gateway, not live yet
- [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/)the Citadel deploy kit
- [Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/)every app answers “present”
- [ADVISOR](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/)the stack's MCP server
- [Booster](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/)upgrades PHP and Laravel

---

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html

## Changelog[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changelog)

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

### \[Unreleased\][#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#unreleased)

- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES S20 (CAS single logout) is tagged `Documented`, not `Not yet`: Academica never sends single logout, and the entry already says apps rely on SESAME's session timeouts (S5).

### \[0.6.1\] - 2026-11-08[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-6-1-2026-11-08)

- Fixed: SESAME's routes are controller actions instead of closures, so `php artisan route:cache` and `optimize` work in an app that uses SESAME (a Citadel release runs optimize).
- Docs: the README and the wayne-cas guide say Booster 1.12.0 and later write `waynestate/sesame:^0.6` (an app hopped by an earlier Booster takes the 0.5.0 and 0.6.0 upgrade steps), and BEST_PRACTICES S45 is `Checked` now that Squire's CI fails if its kit `php.ini` sets `session.sid_length` or `session.sid_bits_per_character`.
- Changed: the deploy layer runs Squire's kit 0.7.1 (was 0.6.0): `.squire/php.ini` no longer sets the deprecated `session.sid_*` lines, web requests get a `disable_functions` list and Apache hardening (`.squire/php-web.ini`, `.squire/apache-hardening.conf`), and opcache gets production settings with `SQUIRE_OPCACHE_VALIDATE` as the one switch.
- Changed: the front page deploy layer requires HELMET ^1.0 (lock at 1.0.1, was 0.4.0), like the rest of the stack; its shared front controller already runs on HELMET 1.0 in Squire, Sourdough and Pinstripe.
- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES S44 now asks for `Clear-Site-Data: "cache", "storage"` and says why `"cookies"` stays out on a shared host, so the row is `Enforced`; S48 describes the Preflight pins as they are (four components at the `@0.3.1` release tag) and is `Checked`, since PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns on an unpinned include.
- Changed: the local a11y scripts run Preflight's own checker (vendored from 0.3.1 and pinned by a test), so they check what CI checks: axe-core 4.14.0, 320 and 1280 px, and the reflow check.

### \[0.6.0\] - 2026-11-08[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-6-0-2026-11-08)

- Added: CI runs Preflight's a11y component (0.3.1) on site/, every page in light and dark at 320 and 1280 px with the WCAG 1.4.10 reflow check, blocking.
- Changed: CI pins the Preflight components to 0.3.1 (fixed cache keys, and caches saved even when a job fails; D-072).
- Changed: CI saves its Composer and npm caches even when a job fails, so a retry after a dropped download fetches only what is missing (D-072).
- Changed: CI caches Composer and npm downloads under a fixed key, so a lock change downloads only what changed (D-072).
- Added: RFC 7662 token introspection for opaque bearer tokens in the `oauth2` driver, behind `oauth2.introspection_url` (env `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_URL`). When set, the driver posts a non-JWT bearer token to the endpoint with `oauth2.introspection_client_id` and `oauth2.introspection_client_secret` (env `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_ID` and `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_SECRET`) as HTTP Basic auth (client id and secret form-encoded first, as RFC 6749 2.3.1 requires), accepts only a `200` JSON answer whose `active` field is `true`, and applies the configured issuer, audience, expiry and not-before checks to the claims it returns. The URL must be `https://` (`http://localhost` and `http://127.0.0.1` are allowed for tests), and the client id and secret are required when it is set.
- Added: `oauth2.introspection_cache_ttl_seconds` (env `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, default `60`, maximum `300`; zero disables the cache), which caps how long an accepted introspection answer is kept under a SHA-256 hash of the token; the raw token is never cached, and a numeric `exp` claim shortens the lifetime further.
- Changed: BEST_PRACTICES S36 moves to `Enforced`: the oauth2 driver's JWT checks and its new RFC 7662 introspection path are both covered by tests.
- Docs: the README, configuration reference, Laravel guide and oauth2 with Entra guide cover the four new introspection settings.
- Fixed: the docs menu closes with Escape and hands focus back to its button (docs kit synced from Squire).
- Fixed: the docs kit's copy button no longer covers the first line of code when it says Copied or Failed: over the code it keeps its resting width and shows a check or a cross when the word does not fit (docs kit synced from Squire).
- Docs: MAINTAINING.md says saml ships (opt-in); BEST_PRACTICES.md is dated 2026-11-08 and drops the answered composer-audit question.
- Changed: the deploy layer requires PROCTOR ^0.8 (locked 0.8.0).
- Added: the native session leaves a "logged out at" marker in the session store when `invalidate()` retires a session (the `logoutReuseTtlSeconds` option of `new NativeSession()` sets the window, 60 seconds by default, `0` destroys the session outright instead); a request that presents that ID gets a fresh empty session, and while the marker is inside the window it logs `sesame.session_anomaly` with `reason` `logged_out_session_reused` once per reuse (BEST_PRACTICES S27).
- Docs: the README art shows `saml` as shipped and opt-in (D-058): the README art kit now re-takes the front page's reference photos in `site/screenshots/` itself, so the gallery's pegboard tags saml Opt-in, as the page does, instead of "later" from a photo taken before the driver shipped. The gallery alt text and `site/README.md` say the same.
- Changed: the pipeline pins every Preflight CI component to 0.3.0 ([preflight@0.3.0](mailto:preflight@0.3.0)); component image inputs are plain image names, since Preflight adds the Dependency Proxy prefix itself.
- Fixed: the Vue adapter's logout() sends Laravel's CSRF token as \_token (from , or the new csrfToken option), so signing out from a Vue page works in Laravel, not only in raw PHP (SESAME-7b).
- Added: a vue job in the GitLab pipeline runs the Vue adapter's tests and type check.
- Docs: a decision page for the 60 second regenerate grace (why, how to turn it off with `graceSeconds: 0`, what is logged after it).
- Fixed: the pipeline's PROCTOR jobs no longer pass `--policy`, which PROCTOR 0.7 refuses in CI; PROCTOR checks against the CREED policy it bundles.
- Changed: the GitLab pipeline pins the Preflight components to 0.2.0 (was 0.1.4).
- Changed: the front page's deploy layer (`deploy/`) runs Squire's kit 0.6.0 (was 0.5.0): `scripts/release.sh` asks PROCTOR's deploy gate for a go or no-go on each release (a report, not a stop, unless `SQUIRE_PROCTOR=enforce`), and `.env.squire.example` lists the new setting. The layer's pins move to HELMET `^0.4` (locked 0.4.0) and PROCTOR `^0.7` (locked 0.7.0).
- Docs: the Docker commands in the README and docs mount the shared `stack-composer-cache` volume, so Composer downloads are cached between runs.
- Fixed: the front page stamp reads 0.5 (it said 0.2), and its stack ring says Sourdough starts all five app shapes, not raw PHP only.
- Fixed: the README and the moving-from-wayne-cas guide name the constraint Booster's `cas-to-sesame` hop writes today, `waynestate/sesame:^0.4` (they said `^0.3`), and point at the 0.5.0 upgrade steps to take after the hop.
- Added: the `saml` driver (SESAME-5), a SAML 2.0 service provider for a Shibboleth-style IdP, opt-in. It stands on `onelogin/php-saml` (suggested, not required; the choice is in `docs/saml-library-choice.md`) in strict mode, requires a signed assertion, refuses SHA-1, IdP-initiated responses and replayed assertion IDs, binds each Response to the AuthnRequest this browser's session holds, checks the IssueInstant against the injected clock, and sends and honors RelayState only through the `ReturnTo` rule. The IdP's cross-site POST is parked in the PSR-16 cache under a single-use handle and checked on the 303's GET, where the `SameSite=Lax` session cookie is back. IdP metadata comes from an https URL or a file, certificates and the SP key from file paths, and no default IdP is assumed. Step-up sends `ForceAuthn`; logout is local.
- Added: `config/sesame.php`'s `saml` block and the `SESAME_SAML_*` settings; the Laravel adapter's `POST /login/saml/acs` (`sesame.saml.acs`) and `GET /login/saml/metadata` (`sesame.saml.metadata`) routes, outside the `web` group; the raw-PHP `sesame_saml_acs()` and `sesame_saml_metadata()`; `sesame_login()` treats `saml_handle` as a ticket.
- Security: SESAME-22: `composer.json` conflicts with `onelogin/php-saml` below 4.3.2 and `robrichards/xmlseclibs` below 3.1.5, the saml driver refuses them at boot, and a test fails when the installed versions are below that floor.
- Tests: a fixture IdP signs responses at runtime with a committed TEST-ONLY key pair (`tests/fixtures/saml`), with negative tests for unsigned, wrongly signed, tampered, wrong audience, issuer, destination and recipient, expired, replayed, unsolicited, SHA-1, DOCTYPE, wrapping and second-signature responses.
- Docs: "The saml driver (SAML 2.0 sign-in)" guide and "The saml driver's library choice"; the drivers, configuration, API, install, troubleshooting, Laravel and raw PHP pages cover the driver; BEST_PRACTICES S34, S35 and S47 move to `Enforced`.
- Changed: CI caches Composer downloads per lock file (`.composer-cache`, keyed on `composer.lock` and `deploy/composer.lock`), so a pipeline stops fetching every package from Packagist on every run. Images already come through the Dependency Proxy.

### \[0.5.0\] - 2026-11-07[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-5-0-2026-11-07)

- Added: `gateway.jwks_file` (env `SESAME_GATEWAY_JWKS_FILE`), a path to a JWKS file of the gateway's public keys by `kid`, the file Drawbridge's `keys:jwks` publishes (its current key and its next). It is read at boot through firebase/php-jwt's JWK parser, and a missing file, private key material, a repeated `kid`, more than 8 keys or a key of the wrong type for `gateway.algorithm` stops the app with `InvalidConfig`. Set one of `public_key`, `public_keys` and `jwks_file`.
- Changed: with exactly one key listed (`public_keys` or `jwks_file`), an assertion with no `kid` is verified with that key instead of refused; a `kid` that names another key is still refused, and with two or more keys a missing `kid` is still refused. `gateway.public_key` still ignores `kid`.
- Docs: the gateway driver guide covers the key set file and the rotation from the app's side.
- Added: `vue/`: the Vue adapter for single-page apps (`useSesame`, `createSesame`), not yet published to npm; a contract test keeps it in step with the status answer.
- Added: BEST_PRACTICES S38: the written rule for Composer audit ignores (who adds one, the reason and review date it carries, and when it must go).
- Changed: The canonical repository is git.wayne.edu (ADR-0021); docs, links and package metadata no longer point at the archived nougat copy.
- Added: the Proof page records its last run.
- Changed: BEST_PRACTICES re-check: S18 moves to `Enforced` (the cas login binding is built), S36 moves to `Partly enforced` (the oauth2 driver enforces the JWT checks; the RFC 7662 introspection path is still open) and S40 moves to `Enforced` (the wayne-cas shim is built as a thin adapter over the core).
- Security: the front-page deploy layer moves to Symfony 7.4.23 (symfony/http-foundation and symfony/yaml advisories, including CVE-2026-118514).
- Added: the Wayne Auth bridge, `Waynestate\Sesame\WayneAuth\WayneAuth`, deprecated on arrival. Apps on the old Wayne Auth SSO cookie keep `new WayneAuth($config)`, `authenticateSSO()`, `getAccessID()` and `_parseSSOCookie('v')`, and sign people in through SESAME's cas driver instead; the one code change is the line that loaded the old class, which now requires the app's SESAME config file calling `WayneAuth::boot()`. Guests go to CAS from inside `authenticateSSO()` (or get `false` with `on_guest => deny`), a ticket that does not validate throws `AuthenticationFailed` rather than looping, the password mode (`'d'`) throws because CAS never releases the password, and `accessid_case` fixes the AccessID's case for apps that compare it. `boot()` refuses to start while the old class is still loaded, and re-reads SESAME's session values for apps that start the session before Composer's autoloader.
- Docs: a "Moving off Wayne Auth" guide (the one-line swap, the options, the call-by-call differences, the checks before shipping and the native next step), linked from "Moving from wayne-cas", the API reference and the README.
- Tests: the bridge is covered against the real cas driver on the fake HTTP client, and a fixture page written the Wayne Auth way signs in end to end under PHP's built-in server.
- Changed: The Laravel guide says Laravel 13 apps must implement `RefreshesUser`, because JSON sessions hand back the stored user as an array.
- Docs: the docs pages sit closer to the front page. The light out of the open door now falls behind each page's title (opening once when motion is allowed), the Overview's picture of the shop hangs in a slate frame, and the badges sit in a row. The after-hours dark mode moved off the green-black floor to a warm dark bench: green stays where the front page puts it (the counter footer, the Open sign, the mark), and inline code and callout colors follow the theme in dark.
- Docs: the docs pages wear the front page's key shop. The same shop sign and main menu (Docs marked current, the Open sign hung on its strings), Bungee titles with a brass key under each, kicker labels, slate code slabs with the gold Copy button, notes and callouts as paper key tags, job-ticket pager and the green counter footer. A derived after-hours dark mode, and motion only when the system allows it. The project name reads SESAME in page titles.
- Changed: NativeSession keeps the old session for a 60 second grace after regenerate (marked with a destroyed-at time), then rejects its reuse and logs sesame.session_anomaly; pass graceSeconds: 0 for the old immediate delete (S43). Laravel is unchanged.
- Changed: the cas driver binds each sign-in to the browser that started it: it stores a pending-login marker in the app's session before the redirect to CAS, and a returning ticket is accepted only against a live marker (single use, ten minutes). A ticket with no live marker is refused before any HTTP call, which blocks login CSRF. Apps that build the driver by hand must pass the app's SessionPort to `DriverFactory::make()`, and an app that must accept a ticket for a login it did not start (a link from the CAS login page) must set `cas.require_pending_login` to false.
- Added: `cas.require_pending_login` (env `SESAME_CAS_REQUIRE_PENDING_LOGIN`, default `true`) switches the cas login binding off.
- Tests: the cas login binding is covered end to end: a ticket with no marker, an expired marker, a reused marker, the natural start-and-return flow, the five-marker cap, the switch off, and the missing-session refusal.
- Added: `Sesame::sessionStatus()`, the session facts a single-page app needs (who, driver, sign-in time, idle and absolute expiry, the logout token), with an optional closure that adds the app's own user fields. The raw PHP function, the Laravel route and the Vue package follow.
- Added: `sesame_status()` (raw PHP) and `GET /sesame/status` (Laravel), the JSON answer a single-page app reads to see who is signed in (200 with the session facts, 401 when signed out, never cacheable); `authenticatedAt` and `authTime` in `sessionStatus()` are now always UTC.
- Docs: the docs site is built by the shared builder and checked in `composer ci`.
- Docs: the docs site now exists. Squire's docs builder renders `docs/` into `site/docs/`: an Overview page from the README's opening, the oidc library choice note, and a generated environment reference table covering all 55 `SESAME_*` settings. `composer docs` builds it, and `composer docs:check` gates it in CI.
- Docs: the README session cookie section also says to leave `session.sid_length` and `session.sid_bits_per_character` at PHP's defaults; BEST_PRACTICES S45 is `Documented`.
- Added: `sesame.session_anomaly`, a warning event for sessions whose state looks wrong or tampered with, apart from the normal timeout logouts. `Sesame::user()` logs it with `reason` `missing_timestamps` (a user stored without the session's timestamps; the session is signed out right after, so the anomaly precedes the `sesame.logout`) or `bad_session_ref` (a stored `sesame.session_ref` that is not a 16-character lowercase hex string; the user stays signed in and the bad value is never echoed into the log). A session without a reference at all is not an anomaly.
- Changed: the front-page deploy layer pins HELMET ^0.3, PROCTOR ^0.4 and CREED ^0.1 (lock: HELMET 0.3.0, PROCTOR 0.4.0, CREED 0.1.6).
- Changed: CI pins Preflight 0.1.4 (GitLab component includes and the GitHub reusable workflow at its tag commit); the deploy layer sets minimum-stability to stable.
- Docs: a "session cookie (name and SameSite)" paragraph in the raw PHP section tells apps to use a `__Host-` cookie name and `SameSite=Lax` (never `Strict`, which drops the cookie on the return from the identity provider), says HELMET sets both for raw PHP, and gives the Laravel settings; BEST_PRACTICES S4 and S41 are now `Documented`.
- Docs: SESAME fails closed on a redirect and on a client exception during the CAS validation call, and tests were added to prove it (S42).
- Docs: a "Refusing a sign-in" section says what a resolver does on a deny, and the CERT Polska CVE-2026-15243 check is recorded (Java clients only; no PHP client named).
- Added: `scripts/a11y.sh` (Linux, macOS) and `scripts/a11y.ps1` (Windows), a site accessibility gate that runs axe-core with the WCAG 2.2 AA tag set against the committed front page and every docs page, in light and dark at two widths, inside Docker so no host browser is needed.
- Fixed: code blocks on the docs pages are keyboard focusable (`tabindex="0"`), so a block that scrolls sideways on a narrow screen can be reached and scrolled from the keyboard (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`). The docs builder adds the attribute; the pages were rebuilt.
- Fixed: "On this page" sub-items on the docs pages carry the base item classes again, so the kit's block link styles apply and the links meet the minimum target size (axe `target-size`). The docs builder sets both classes; the pages were rebuilt.

### \[0.4.0\] - 2026-11-03[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-4-0-2026-11-03)

- This is a pre-1.0 minor: apps that pin `^0.3` stay on 0.3.x until they move their constraint to `^0.4`. The `gateway` driver now refuses a token whose `typ` header is `at+jwt`, so read the Security line first.
- Docs: the cas quick start's Guzzle client now sets `allow_redirects` to false and `verify` to true, with a note that PSR-18 has no standard option for either (S42).
- Added: `session_ref`, a per sign-in correlation id that ties the auth events of one sign-in together in the log. `Sesame::login()` creates a fresh 16-character lowercase hex reference and stores it in the session under `sesame.session_ref`, and `sesame.login` and `sesame.logout` carry it in their context. It is not the session ID and never derived from it; a value read back from the session that is not a 16-character lowercase hex string is ignored, so a tampered session cannot inject log text.
- Added: `Identity::isFromNewLogin()` and `Identity::usedLongTermToken()` read the CAS `isFromNewLogin` and `longTermAuthenticationRequestTokenUsed` attributes (`true`, `false`, or `null` when the server did not say or sent anything else), so an app can tell a fresh login from a remembered one.
- Added: optional PSR-3 logging of authentication events. `Sesame` takes an optional sixth constructor argument, and the Laravel adapter passes the app's logger when the container has one; `sesame.log` (env `SESAME_LOG`, default `true`) turns the events off. The events are `sesame.login`, `sesame.login_failed`, `sesame.login_refused` and `sesame.logout`, each carrying `event`, `driver`, `username` and `at` in its context (`reason` on logout); tickets, session IDs, tokens and failure messages are never logged.
- Added: `oauth2.require_at_jwt` (env `SESAME_OAUTH2_REQUIRE_AT_JWT`), an opt-in check that the access token's `typ` header is `at+jwt` or `application/at+jwt`. It is off by default because Microsoft Entra v2 access tokens are typed `JWT`, so requiring it would refuse every Entra token.
- Security: the `gateway` driver refuses a token whose `typ` header is `at+jwt` or `application/at+jwt`, so an OAuth2 access token cannot be replayed as a gateway assertion. A missing `typ` or `JWT` still works.
- Docs: BEST_PRACTICES tags now match the code: the entries whose fix is already in `src/` and `tests/` are re-tagged (`Enforced`, `Documented` or `Partly enforced`) with the code and test file:line named, and the gap list at the bottom drops the items that are closed.
- Docs: the "Moving from wayne-cas" section now leads with the easy way, Booster's `cas-to-sesame` hop (planned with `--sesame`, needs the plan to end on PHP 8.3 or newer), then the by-hand mapping, then what Booster leaves for you (Duo 2FA is not carried, verify login on the pre-production host).
- Docs: the cas quick start's Guzzle client now sets a `timeout` and `connect_timeout` (Guzzle has no total timeout by default), and the oauth2 quick start does the same.
- Docs: a "Which key to store" paragraph tells apps to key their users on the driver plus the identity provider's stable identifier, never an email or a display name.
- Docs: a note tells apps to log `AuthenticationFailed` messages and show the user one generic line, since the message can carry the CAS failure code.
- Added: `gateway.public_keys`, a map of `kid` to public key, so the gateway driver can verify against two keys at once (the assertion's `kid` header picks the key) for key rotation without a coordinated window.
- Changed: CI pulls its Docker Hub images through the GitLab Dependency Proxy (the group's CI_DEPENDENCY_PROXY_GROUP_IMAGE_PREFIX), so pipelines no longer hit Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit.
- Changed: docs and package metadata name nougat as the canonical repository, with git.wayne.edu and GitHub as read-only mirrors, until git.wayne.edu has CI runners.

### \[0.3.0\] - 2026-10-30[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-3-0-2026-10-30)

- Security: the signed-in user is looked up again on every request when the app's resolver implements the new `RefreshesUser` interface, and a user who no longer exists signs the session out. Before, `Sesame::user()` returned the copy saved at sign-in, so a user whose role was removed kept it until the session ended. The wayne-cas `UserResolver` implements it (a plain find by primary key, never an import).
- Added: a `sesame` Laravel guard driver. Set `auth.guards.web.driver` to `sesame` and the users provider to `eloquent`, and `auth()->user()` returns the SESAME user; a Laravel login, `onceUsingId()` or `actingAs()` still wins for the request.
- Fixed: the wayne-cas `WayneAuthenticate` middleware lets SESAME's login, callback and logout routes through, so it is safe in the global `web` group (it used to send `/login` to itself forever).
- Fixed: the wayne-cas `WayneCasable` interface and `ReadOnlyAttributes` trait agree on one signature, `public function getReadOnlyAttributes($persistedAttributes = []): array`. Models need that exact method (public, with the parameter).
- Fixed: resolving SESAME no longer builds the driver, so guests on http, artisan commands, queue workers and tests can ask who is signed in; the driver (and its https check) is built when someone signs in or out.
- Changed: the missing `sesame.user_resolver` error names the wayne-cas resolver class.
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.4 (the local .env.squire file is now git-ignored).

### \[0.2.2\] - 2026-10-29[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-2-2026-10-29)

- Changed: README leads with the gateway driver for Citadel apps and labels the oidc driver as the exception that needs its own Entra registration.
- Changed: the deploy layer's Squire kit is refreshed to 0.3.3 (release options can now live in ./.env.squire).
- Fixed: the oidc driver's default roles claim is wsu_roles, the name Entra sends; set roles_claim (and claims) to wsuRoles to keep the old name. Apps that relied on the old default must set it.

### \[0.2.0\] - 2026-10-29[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-2-0-2026-10-29)

- Changed: the proof page moves to a private site that needs a Wayne State sign-in.

#### Added[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added)

- The `oidc` driver: browser sign-in with OpenID Connect (authorization code flow with PKCE S256, `state` and `nonce` bound to the session, single use, ten-minute expiry), Microsoft Entra ID first. Discovery and the key set are cached through PSR-16 for `oidc.cache_ttl_seconds` (default and maximum 3600) and each endpoint can be overridden; the ID token is checked for signature (RS256 by default, never `none` or HMAC), `iss`, `aud`, `azp`, `exp`, `nbf`, `iat` and `nonce`. No `prompt` or `max_age` by default (silent SSO); `step_up=1` adds the configured step-up parameters and requires a fresh `auth_time` (never in the future, and within `max_age`, 300 seconds when none is configured). Username from `accessid` (the `preferred_username` fallback is an opt-in, off by default, because users can change that claim), `iss`, `sub`, `tid` and `oid` passed to the resolver as stable account keys, roles from `wsuRoles`, MFA from `auth_time` and `amr` (or `oidc.assume_mfa`), and the claims in `SESAME_OIDC_CLAIMS` (default `wsuRoles,accessid`) passed to the resolver as attributes. Optional logout through Entra with `post_logout_redirect_uri`. Token, discovery and key-set requests never follow a redirect: a 3xx answer is an error (`oidc.token_redirect`, `oidc.discovery_unavailable`, `oidc.jwks_unavailable`), so the code, verifier and secret cannot be resent elsewhere. See "The oidc driver (Entra sign-in)".
- The oidc driver stands on `league/oauth2-client` (suggested, not required; a clear error names the install command when it is missing) for the OAuth mechanics, and on SESAME's own firebase/php-jwt key-set code for the ID token. Why: `docs/oidc-library-choice.md`.
- Laravel: `GET /login/callback` (`sesame.callback`) for the oidc driver, the redirect URI defaulting to it, and `sesame.mfa` reauth asking the provider for a step-up.
- `Sesame::returnTo()` and the `RemembersReturnTo` interface, so `sesame_login()` and the Laravel route send the user to the checked return-to address after a callback.
- `Setting::env()`, and `SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` read from the environment only, never from the playbook. The secret is held in a `SensitiveParameterValue` (hidden from `var_export`, `json_encode`, dumps and array casts; `serialize` refuses), and the parameters that carry it, the ID token, the code or the PKCE verifier are marked `#[\SensitiveParameter]`.
- README: a loud note that raw-PHP apps must raise `session.gc_maxlifetime` to at least SESAME's idle timeout.

#### Changed[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed)

- Raw PHP: `sesame_logout()` is POST-only with a CSRF token. It runs only when the POST body's `sesame_logout_token` matches the session's token (new `sesame_logout_token()`, `Sesame::logoutToken()` and `Sesame::isLogoutToken()`); a GET answers 405 and a bad token 403, and neither touches the session. Apps must change a logout link to a POST form carrying the token. The Laravel `POST /logout` route stays in the `web` group and so under Laravel's CSRF check, now covered by a test.
- Laravel: the Guzzle client SESAME builds when the app binds none has redirects off.
- `ReturnTo` (every driver's login and logout return-to) now requires the service URL's scheme, host and effective port, and refuses a URL with a user name or password; before, the host alone was compared, so `https://app.example.test:8443/` passed for a service on 443. Plain http is accepted only for a localhost or 127.0.0.1 service URL.
- `DriverFactory::make()` takes the app session as an optional seventh argument (the oidc driver needs it).
- `JwksProvider` takes the algorithm per key lookup and a reason prefix, so the oauth2 and oidc drivers share it.
- `JwksProvider`: the first (cold) key-set fetch no longer starts the one-minute refetch cooldown, so a key rotated just after it is picked up by the next unknown key id (oauth2 and oidc).

### \[0.1.3\] - 2026-10-29[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-3-2026-10-29)

#### Added[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added-1)

- The four shared WSU values (`SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL`, `SESAME_GATEWAY_ISSUER`, `SESAME_OAUTH2_ISSUER`, `SESAME_OAUTH2_JWKS_URL`) now resolve through `Waynestate\Sesame\Support\Setting::get()`: the environment wins, and when it is empty the private `waynestate/playbook` package supplies the value. `waynestate/playbook` is suggested, never required.
- A missing routed setting now fails with `Missing required setting SESAME_.... Set it in the environment, or install waynestate/playbook (see the README).` instead of naming the config key.

### \[0.1.2\] - 2026-10-29[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-2-2026-10-29)

#### Fixed[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#fixed)

- The CAS driver reads `serviceValidate` responses by namespace URI instead of prefix: a body that binds the `cas:` prefix to a different namespace can no longer be read as a success, while a body that binds another prefix (or none) to the real CAS namespace keeps working.

### \[0.1.1\] (2026-10-29)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-1-2026-10-29)

#### Added[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#added-2)

- Step-up by authentication context: the gateway driver reads the signed assertion's `acrs` claim (authentication context ids `c1` through `c99`, anything else dropped) and carries the contexts on the `Identity`.
- `Identity::authContexts()` and `Identity::hasAuthContext(string $id)`: membership in the context list, never a prefix match.
- `Sesame::hasAuthContext(string $id)`: the context check against the current session, failing closed when there is no user or no identity.
- `sesame_require_context(string $id)` for the raw-PHP path: returns the app's user when the identity has the context, throws `AuthContextNotSatisfied` when it does not.
- The `sesame.context` Laravel middleware (`sesame.context:c1`): lets the request through when the identity has the context, answers 403 otherwise, and a JSON 403 with a `message` for JSON requests. A route without a context parameter fails closed.
- `AuthContextNotSatisfied`, the exception for a failed context check, carrying the context id.
- `cas.assume_mfa` (default `false`): when the CAS server enforces MFA for every sign-in, a successful validation then counts as an MFA sign-in. The identity's `amr` includes `mfa`, and its MFA time comes from the CAS `authenticationDate` attribute; without one, the MFA check fails with `NO_AUTH_TIME` instead of inventing a sign-in time.
- `DriverFactory::make()` with the gateway driver throws `InvalidConfig` naming the key when `gateway.public_key`, `gateway.issuer` or `gateway.audience` is null or empty, instead of passing an empty string into the driver.
- A truthy `slo` (or `single_logout`) config key is rejected with `InvalidConfig` at boot: the identity provider does not support single logout, so the setting is a mistake to fail on early rather than at the first logout.
- The `oauth2` driver: signs the user in from a JWT bearer token in the `Authorization` header, verified against the issuer's key set (a JWKS) fetched over HTTP. Only RS256 tokens are accepted; a token that claims `none` or an HMAC algorithm is refused before its signature is looked at. After the signature, the driver checks the issuer, audience, `exp` and `nbf` claims (with a leeway), then any required scopes (against the `scp` claim) and roles (against the `roles` claim). Microsoft Entra ID is the first planned issuer; any other RS256 issuer works with the same settings.
- `oauth2` config keys: `oauth2.issuer`, `oauth2.jwks_url` and `oauth2.audience` (all required), `oauth2.leeway_seconds` (default `60`), `oauth2.required_scopes` and `oauth2.required_roles` (default empty, which checks nothing), `oauth2.identity_claim` (`preferred_username` or `accessid`, default `preferred_username`), and `oauth2.jwks_cache_ttl_seconds` (default `3600`).
- `JwksProvider`: keeps the fetched key set in a PSR-16 cache for `oauth2.jwks_cache_ttl_seconds`, refetches at most once a minute when a token carries an unknown key id (so a rotated key is picked up without hammering the issuer), and fails closed on an unreachable issuer, a non-2xx answer, or an empty or malformed key set.
- The Laravel adapter wires the oauth2 driver: the PSR-18 client comes from the app's `ClientInterface` binding or Guzzle, and the key set cache comes from the app's cache, using the store named by `oauth2.jwks_store` (the default store when none is named).
- `firebase/php-jwt` as a dependency: JWKS parsing and RS256 verification come from the library, not from SESAME's own code.

#### Changed[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#changed-1)

- Static analysis now includes Pinstripe's `phpstan/strict.neon` preset from the `waynestate/pinstripe` dev dependency instead of the hand-copied settings: PHPStan level 8, deprecation checks on, strict rules stay on. No behaviour changed.

### \[0.1.0\] (2026-10-27)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#0-1-0-2026-10-27)

- First tagged release.

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html

## The cas driver[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#the-cas-driver)

This page sets up the `cas` driver, which signs a user in against a CAS server, CAS 2.0 against Academica by default, with no per-app Entra registration. Start with the config below, then read the behavior notes for the options you plan to change.

![SESAME's key duplicator tracing the cas key: five notches, one per sign-in step, and logout at the tip](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/duplicator.svg)

The duplicator traces the cas key from the front page: five notches, one per sign-in step, and logout at the tip. The cut is the sign-in; the lock is still yours. With reduced motion on, you get the finished key.

### Configure the driver[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#configure-the-driver)

The cas driver logs in against a CAS server, CAS 2.0 by default. The base URL is required config with no default, and it must include the path the CAS server lives under. For Academica, which serves CAS under `/cas`, it is `https://login.wayne.edu/cas`.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Nyholm\Psr7\Factory\Psr17Factory;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Config;
use Waynestate\Sesame\DriverFactory;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Session\NativeSession;

$config = Config::fromArray([
    'driver' => 'cas',
    'environment' => 'production',
    'cas' => [
        'base_url' => 'https://login.wayne.edu/cas',
        'service_url' => 'https://app.apps.wayne.edu/login',
    ],
]);

// Any PSR-18 client works, for example Guzzle. Set a timeout: Guzzle has no
// total timeout by default, so a hung CAS server would hold the request open
// forever. Turn redirects off for the validation call (Guzzle follows up to
// five by default, to any host or to plain http) and leave TLS verification
// on (`verify` is true by default; never set it to false). PSR-18 has no
// standard option for either, so the client you hand SESAME must carry them.
// SESAME treats any non-200 answer (including a redirect) as a failed login
// and lets a client exception through, so a client that is set up wrong fails
// the sign-in and never signs anyone in.
$http = new \GuzzleHttp\Client([
    'timeout' => 10,
    'connect_timeout' => 5,
    'allow_redirects' => false,
    'verify' => true,
]);

// The app's session, seen through the port. The cas driver keeps its
// pending-login marker there (see "Binding the sign-in to the browser" below).
$session = new NativeSession();

$driver = DriverFactory::make($config, $http, new Psr17Factory(), null, null, null, $session);
```

Then build the Sesame facade with the driver and the same session, as in the Raw PHP section of the README.

### Config keys[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#config-keys)

| Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cas.base_url` | Yes | none | The CAS server, an absolute https:// URL, including the path the CAS server lives under (for Academica, `/cas`). |
| `cas.service_url` | Yes | none | Where the server sends the user back to. |
| `cas.protocol` | No | `2.0` | `3.0` or `2.0`. |
| `cas.renew` | No | `false` | Send `renew` on login and validation, so the CAS server requires a fresh, direct login. |
| `cas.assume_mfa` | No | `false` | A successful validation counts as an MFA sign-in: the identity's `amr` includes `mfa`. On only when the CAS server enforces MFA for every sign-in. |
| `cas.require_pending_login` | No | `true` | Bind each sign-in to the browser that started it (blocks login CSRF). Off only for an app that must accept a ticket for a login it did not start, a link from the CAS login page. |

The service URL is the configured value only: the driver never reads the request's Host or X-Forwarded-\* headers to build it.

### Protocol[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#protocol)

Protocol 2.0 is the default because Academica is believed to redirect cookieless `/p3/serviceValidate` calls to the login page. Set `cas.protocol` to `3.0` when a CAS server releases attributes on `/p3/serviceValidate`.

### Renew[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#renew)

Set `cas.renew` to `true` when the app needs a fresh, direct login rather than an existing SSO session. The driver then sends `renew` on the login redirect and on the validation request, and the CAS server refuses a ticket that came from an SSO session with `INVALID_TICKET`. Leave it off against Academica: it does not issue a ticket for `renew=true` and sends the user back to the login page, so a `renew` login loops instead of signing in.

### Sign-in time[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#sign-in-time)

The sign-in time on the identity comes from the CAS `authenticationDate` attribute when the server sends one. When it is missing, unparseable, or more than five minutes ahead of the driver's clock, the driver uses its own clock instead, so a bad value can never push the sign-in time into the future.

With `cas.protocol` set to `3.0`, a server may also release `isFromNewLogin` and `longTermAuthenticationRequestTokenUsed`. The identity reads them as `$identity->isFromNewLogin()` and `$identity->usedLongTermToken()`: `true` or `false` when the server said so (any letter case), and `null` when the attribute is missing or is anything but `true` or `false`. SESAME never guesses, so an app that wants a fresh login for a sensitive action can check `isFromNewLogin() === true` and send the user back through `cas.renew` when it is anything else.

### MFA[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#mfa)

`cas.assume_mfa` is off by default, and it should stay off unless the CAS server enforces MFA for every sign-in. A successful CAS validation then means MFA happened for the user's current SSO session, and the driver says so on the identity: its `amr` includes `mfa`. Ask your CAS server's owner before turning it on; a server that enforces MFA only sometimes, or only for some users, would make the MFA check pass for sign-ins that never did MFA.

The MFA age still needs a sign-in time, and the driver never invents one: it comes from the CAS `authenticationDate` attribute, and when the server does not send one, the MFA check fails because there is no sign-in time to age.

### Binding the sign-in to the browser[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#binding-the-sign-in-to-the-browser)

With `cas.require_pending_login` on (the default), the driver stores a marker in the app's session before it sends the browser to CAS, and a returning ticket is accepted only against a live marker. The marker is single use and lives ten minutes, and the session keeps at most five of them, one per open sign-in tab, newest kept. A ticket with no live marker is refused before any HTTP call to the CAS server, which blocks login CSRF: an attacker who signs in through CAS for their own account cannot make a victim's browser deliver the attacker's ticket, because the victim's session holds no marker.

The driver needs the app's session for the marker, so pass it to `DriverFactory::make()` as the seventh argument (the example above passes a `NativeSession`). Set `cas.require_pending_login` to `false` only for an app that must accept a ticket for a login it did not start, for example a link from the CAS login page itself; that reopens login CSRF, so keep such an opt-out deliberate.

Warning

On a failed login, show a generic line, not the exception. An `AuthenticationFailed` message can carry the CAS failure code (for example `INVALID_TICKET`), which tells an attacker how the server refused the ticket. Log the message for operators and show the user one generic line instead.

### Related[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html#related)

- [Running off Citadel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)
- [The gateway driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html)

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html

## The gateway driver[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#the-gateway-driver)

This page sets up the `gateway` driver, the recommended path on Citadel: it verifies the signed JWT assertion the Drawbridge gateway sends in one header, never a bare identity header. Configure the driver below, then read the key rotation steps before you rotate the gateway's signing key.

Note

Drawbridge is not live yet, so there is no production gateway to point at today. Until it is, CAS (the `cas` driver) is today's option for a Citadel app, and it needs no per-app Entra registration. Once Drawbridge is live, every app behind it uses this driver and needs no Entra registration of its own.

### How it verifies[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#how-it-verifies)

The gateway driver signs the user in from a signed JWT assertion that the auth gateway (Drawbridge) puts in one header. It verifies the assertion's signature against the gateway's public key, then checks the issuer, audience and time claims. It never reads a plain identity header: `Remote-User`, `X-Remote-User`, or any spelling of them, because a plain header can come from anywhere on the shared network. And the request must come from a trusted proxy: the direct peer (`REMOTE_ADDR`) must match one of the configured CIDR ranges. A valid assertion from an untrusted peer is still rejected.

The algorithm is pinned from config, so a token that claims a different algorithm (or `none`) is refused before its signature is even looked at.

Every assertion is single-use. The driver requires a `jti` claim, refuses an assertion that lives longer than `gateway.max_lifetime` seconds, and remembers each `jti` it has seen in a replay guard, so a captured assertion cannot be played back a second time. The guard is a PSR-16 cache: the Laravel adapter wires one up for you, and a raw PHP app passes its own (below).

### Configure the driver[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#configure-the-driver)

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Symfony\Component\Cache\Adapter\FilesystemAdapter;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Config;
use Waynestate\Sesame\DriverFactory;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Drivers\Psr16ReplayGuard;

$config = Config::fromArray([
    'driver' => 'gateway',
    'environment' => 'production',
    'gateway' => [
        'public_key' => file_get_contents('/etc/sesame/gateway.pub'),
        'issuer' => 'https://drawbridge.wayne.edu',
        'audience' => 'sesame',
        'trusted_proxies' => ['10.0.0.0/8'],
    ],
]);

// The gateway driver needs no HTTP client: it only reads the assertion from
// the request. It does need a replay guard, so a captured assertion cannot be
// played back a second time. Any PSR-16 cache works (symfony/cache is shown);
// the Laravel adapter wires one up for you, so you only see this in raw PHP.
$guard = new Psr16ReplayGuard(new FilesystemAdapter());
$driver = DriverFactory::make($config, null, null, null, $guard);
```

Then build the Sesame facade with the driver, as in the Raw PHP section of the README.

### Config keys[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#config-keys)

| Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gateway.header` | No | `X-Sesame-Assertion` | The one header that holds the signed assertion. |
| `gateway.algorithm` | No | `ES256` | `ES256`, `RS256` or `EdDSA`. Pinned, so a token that claims another algorithm is refused. |
| `gateway.public_key` | Yes, unless `public_keys` or `jwks_file` is set | none | The gateway's public key: a PEM string (or a path to one) for `ES256` and `RS256`, or a base64-encoded raw key (or a path to one) for `EdDSA`. |
| `gateway.public_keys` | No | none | A map of `kid` to public key, for rotating the gateway's signing key. |
| `gateway.jwks_file` | No | none | A path to a JWKS file of the gateway's public keys by `kid` (Drawbridge's `keys:jwks` writes it), read at boot. Set one of `public_key`, `public_keys` and `jwks_file`. |
| `gateway.issuer` | Yes | none | The `iss` claim the assertion must carry. |
| `gateway.audience` | Yes | none | The `aud` claim the assertion must carry. |
| `gateway.leeway_seconds` | No | `30` | Clock skew allowed on the `iat`, `nbf` and `exp` checks, in seconds. |
| `gateway.trusted_proxies` | Yes | none | A non-empty array of CIDR ranges (or single IPs) the gateway proxy sits behind. |
| `gateway.max_lifetime` | No | `300` | The longest an assertion may live (`exp` minus `iat`), in seconds. Longer assertions are refused, so a stolen long-lived token is useless. |
| `gateway.replay_store` | No | the app's default cache store | The cache store the used `jti`s are kept in (Laravel only; raw PHP passes its own PSR-16 cache to the guard). |
| `gateway.allow_without_replay_guard` | No | `false` | Skip the replay guard entirely. Local development only: a production app must keep replay protection on. |

### Assertion claims[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#assertion-claims)

The assertion must carry `sub`, `iat`, `exp` and `jti`; the `sub` claim becomes the username. The optional `email`, `name` and `affiliations` claims become read-only identity attributes. The sign-in time on the identity comes from the driver's clock.

The optional `auth_time` and `amr` claims become the identity's MFA facts, for `requireMfa()`. `auth_time` is the epoch seconds of the user's last MFA sign-in; `amr` is the list of methods they used. A missing or malformed `auth_time` leaves the MFA time unset, and a missing or malformed `amr` leaves the method list empty, so a claim the gateway did not verify can never satisfy the check.

### Rotating the gateway's signing key[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#rotating-the-gateway-s-signing-key)

The gateway signs with one key at a time and names it in the `kid` header of every assertion. An app may list several public keys at once, so a key rotation needs no coordinated window. The driver verifies each assertion with the key listed under its `kid`; an unknown `kid` is refused, and so is one signed by another listed key under the wrong `kid`. With two or more keys listed, an assertion with no `kid` is refused; with exactly one, it is verified with that key, so a single-key setup keeps working. The algorithm stays pinned from config for every key.

#### The key set file[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#the-key-set-file)

The easy way to list the keys is the key set file Drawbridge publishes (`bin/drawbridge keys:jwks`): a standard JWKS file that always holds the gateway's current key and its next one. Point `gateway.jwks_file` (or `SESAME_GATEWAY_JWKS_FILE`) at it. Public keys are not secrets, so the file may live in your repository or on a read-only mount.

```dotenv
SESAME_GATEWAY_JWKS_FILE=/var/www/app/config/drawbridge-keys.json
```

SESAME reads the file at boot and stops with an `InvalidConfig` error, before any request is served, when the file:

- is missing, unreadable or larger than 64 KB;
- is not a JWKS document (a JSON object with a non-empty `keys` list) or holds more than 8 keys;
- has a key without a `kid`, or lists a `kid` twice;
- holds any private key material (`d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `oth` or `k`); if this happens, treat that private key as exposed;
- has a key of the wrong type for `gateway.algorithm` (ES256 needs EC P-256, RS256 needs RSA of 2048 bits or more, EdDSA needs OKP Ed25519), or an `alg` or `use` that does not match.

#### A rotation, from the app's side[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#a-rotation-from-the-app-s-side)

1. The gateway switches to its next key. Your app already trusts it, because it was in the file all along: nothing to do.
2. Drawbridge publishes a new file (the new current key and a new next key; the retired key is gone). Deploy it, or refresh the mount, when you can. Until then the old file still works.

Drawbridge's [rotation guide](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/rotating-the-signing-key.html) has the gateway's side and the emergency steps.

#### The same keys in PHP config[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#the-same-keys-in-php-config)

`gateway.public_keys` takes the same keys as a map. Set one of `public_key`, `public_keys` and `jwks_file`, never two.

```php
'gateway' => [
    'public_keys' => [
        'drawbridge-2026-11' => file_get_contents('/etc/sesame/gateway-2026-11.pub'),
        'drawbridge-2027-11' => file_get_contents('/etc/sesame/gateway-2027-11.pub'),
    ],
    // issuer, audience, trusted_proxies and the rest, as before.
],
```

Two keys on the pegboard, one door: while the old one still hangs there, nobody gets locked out.

### Related[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html#related)

- [The cas driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html)
- [Running off Citadel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)
