Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html

## oauth2 with Entra[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html#oauth2-with-entra)

The goal: sign an API in from a JWT bearer token that Microsoft Entra ID (or any other RS256 issuer) has already issued, without a browser round trip. Open sesame, for machines: the lock checks the key against the issuer's own key set, and the door stays yours. Read this page to wire the driver up, then move on to [raw-php.md](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html) to build the facade and start signing in.

### How the driver verifies a token[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html#how-the-driver-verifies-a-token)

The oauth2 driver signs the user in from a JWT bearer token in the `Authorization` header, verified against the issuer's key set (a JWKS) fetched from `oauth2.jwks_url`. Only RS256 tokens are accepted: a token that claims `none` or an HMAC algorithm is refused before its signature is even looked at, and the key used to verify is the one the issuer published under the token's key id, never anything the token itself carries. After the signature, the driver checks the issuer, audience, expiry and not-before claims (with a leeway), then any required scopes and roles.

A token that is not a three-part JWT is opaque while introspection is off, and it is refused. When `oauth2.introspection_url` is set, the driver posts the token to that RFC 7662 endpoint with the configured client credentials as HTTP Basic auth, accepts only a `200` JSON answer whose `active` field is `true`, and applies the same issuer, audience, expiry and not-before checks to the claims the endpoint returns. Accepted answers are cached briefly under a hash of the token; the token itself is never cached or logged.

Microsoft Entra ID is the first supported issuer. Point `issuer` and `jwks_url` at the tenant's v2.0 endpoints (the `issuer` and `jwks_uri` values in the tenant's discovery document) and `audience` at the app's client id. Any other RS256 issuer works with the same settings.

### Setting up the driver[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html#setting-up-the-driver)

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Nyholm\Psr7\Factory\Psr17Factory;
use Symfony\Component\Cache\Adapter\FilesystemAdapter;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Config;
use Waynestate\Sesame\DriverFactory;

$config = Config::fromArray([
    'driver' => 'oauth2',
    'environment' => 'production',
    'oauth2' => [
        'issuer' => 'https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0',
        'jwks_url' => 'https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/discovery/v2.0/keys',
        'audience' => '<client id>',
        'required_scopes' => ['openid'],
    ],
]);

// Any PSR-18 client works, for example Guzzle. Set a timeout: Guzzle has no
// total timeout by default, so a hung issuer would hold the request open
// forever.
$http = new \GuzzleHttp\Client(['timeout' => 10, 'connect_timeout' => 5]);

// Any PSR-16 cache works (symfony/cache is shown); the Laravel adapter wires
// one up for you, so you only see this in raw PHP.
$driver = DriverFactory::make($config, $http, new Psr17Factory(), null, null, new FilesystemAdapter());
```

Then build the Sesame facade with the driver, as in the [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html) page above.

### Config keys[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html#config-keys)

| Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `oauth2.issuer` | Yes | none | The `iss` claim the token must carry. For Entra, the `issuer` value in the tenant's discovery document. |
| `oauth2.jwks_url` | Yes | none | The URL of the issuer's JSON Web Key Set. For Entra, the `jwks_uri` value in the tenant's discovery document. |
| `oauth2.audience` | Yes | none | The `aud` claim the token must carry. For Entra, the app's client id. |
| `oauth2.leeway_seconds` | No | `60` | Clock skew allowed on the `exp` and `nbf` checks, in seconds. |
| `oauth2.required_scopes` | No | `[]` | Scopes the token's `scp` claim must cover, all of them. An empty list checks nothing. |
| `oauth2.required_roles` | No | `[]` | Roles the token's `roles` claim must include, all of them. An empty list checks nothing. |
| `oauth2.identity_claim` | No | `preferred_username` | The claim the username comes from: `preferred_username`, or `accessid` (the UPN's mail prefix, Entra's user claim). |
| `oauth2.jwks_cache_ttl_seconds` | No | `3600` | How long the fetched key set is kept before it is refetched, in seconds. |
| `oauth2.jwks_store` | No | the app's default cache store | The cache store the key set is kept in (Laravel only; raw PHP passes its own PSR-16 cache). |
| `oauth2.require_at_jwt` | No | `false` | When `true`, the token's `typ` header must be `at+jwt` or `application/at+jwt` (RFC 9068), and any other token is refused. **Off by default on purpose:** Microsoft Entra v2 access tokens are typed `JWT`, so turning it on refuses every Entra token. Turn it on only for an identity provider that issues RFC 9068 tokens. |
| `oauth2.introspection_url` | No | none | The RFC 7662 endpoint for opaque bearer tokens: `https://` only (`http://localhost` and `http://127.0.0.1` are allowed for tests). Leave it unset to keep the driver JWT-only. |
| `oauth2.introspection_client_id` | No | none | The client id sent as HTTP Basic auth to the introspection endpoint. Required when `oauth2.introspection_url` is set. |
| `oauth2.introspection_client_secret` | No | none | The client secret sent as HTTP Basic auth to the introspection endpoint. Required when `oauth2.introspection_url` is set. |
| `oauth2.introspection_cache_ttl_seconds` | No | `60` | How long an accepted introspection answer is kept, in seconds, capped by the token's `exp`. Zero disables the cache. |

Warning

Leave `oauth2.require_at_jwt` off for Entra. Microsoft Entra v2 access tokens are typed `JWT`, so requiring `at+jwt` refuses every Entra token. Turn it on only for an identity provider that issues RFC 9068 tokens.

Note

Leave `oauth2.introspection_url` unset for ordinary Entra apps: Entra v2 issues JWTs that the driver verifies locally against the JWKS. Set the introspection keys only when your issuer hands out opaque bearer tokens that need an RFC 7662 check.

### What the token must carry[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html#what-the-token-must-carry)

A JWT must carry an `exp` claim; a JWT without one is refused. The `email` and `name` claims become read-only identity attributes, and the optional `auth_time` and `amr` claims become the identity's MFA facts, for `requireMfa()`, exactly as in the gateway driver.

An accepted introspection answer must carry a usable username: the configured `oauth2.identity_claim` (`preferred_username` by default) or `sub`. Its `iss`, `aud`, `exp` and `nbf` claims are checked when present, with the same leeway as the JWT path.

### Key set caching and fail-closed fetches[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html#key-set-caching-and-fail-closed-fetches)

The key set is fetched once and kept for `oauth2.jwks_cache_ttl_seconds`. When a token carries a key id the cached set does not know, the provider refetches the set once, and at most once a minute, so a rotated key is picked up without hammering the issuer. The first fetch does not start that minute, so a key rotated just after it is still picked up at once. Everything about the fetch fails closed: an unreachable issuer, a non-2xx answer, or an empty or malformed key set all refuse the sign-in rather than let it through.

### Related[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html#related)

- [Which driver for my app?](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/which-driver.html)
- [The oidc driver (Entra sign-in)](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html)
- [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Laravel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)
- [Requiring MFA](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/requiring-mfa.html)

---

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html

## The oidc driver (Entra sign-in)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#the-oidc-driver-entra-sign-in)

The goal: sign a person into your app through the browser, straight at Microsoft Entra ID, with OpenID Connect. This page walks through how a sign-in runs, every config key, and the one-time Entra app registration; then set the driver up on the [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html) or [Laravel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html) page.

Note

This is the exception, not the default. On Citadel prefer the `gateway` driver behind Drawbridge, which needs no Entra registration per app. This driver needs its own registration (see "The Entra app registration" below).

### What you need[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#what-you-need)

Open sesame, said straight to Entra. The oidc driver signs a person in through the browser with OpenID Connect: the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), the ID token checked against the issuer's key set. It is the Entra-direct path beside `cas` and `gateway` (Drawbridge), and it needs `league/oauth2-client`, which SESAME suggests but does not require:

```
composer require league/oauth2-client
```

Without it, building the driver fails with `The oidc driver needs league/oauth2-client. Install it with: composer require league/oauth2-client`. Why that library, and what else was weighed: [docs/oidc-library-choice.md](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/oidc-library-choice.html).

### How a sign-in runs[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#how-a-sign-in-runs)

1. A request to the login URL without a `code` starts it. The driver makes a fresh `state` and `nonce` and a PKCE verifier, keeps all three in the app's session (bound to this browser, single use, gone after ten minutes), and redirects to the authorization endpoint with `response_mode=query`.
2. Entra sends the browser back to the redirect URI with `code` and `state`. The driver takes the pending sign-in for that state out of the session first (a replayed callback finds nothing), exchanges the code with the verifier and the client secret, and validates the ID token: signature against the JWKS (RS256 by default, never `none` or HMAC), `iss` exactly, `aud` is the client id, `azp` when present, `exp`, `nbf` and `iat` with a 60-second leeway, and the `nonce`. No request to the provider (token, discovery, key set) follows a redirect: a 3xx answer fails the sign-in, so the code, the verifier and the secret are never resent elsewhere.
3. The identity goes to the app's `findOrImportUser(Identity)`, and the core regenerates the session ID, as for every driver. The access token and the ID token are never stored.

### Silent SSO and step-up[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#silent-sso-and-step-up)

**SSO stays silent.** No `prompt` and no `max_age` are sent by default, so a person already signed in to Entra (Outlook, Teams, Canvas) is signed in without a click.

**Step-up.** A login request with `step_up=1` adds the app's configured step-up parameters: `prompt=login` by default, and optionally `max_age`, `acr_values` and `claims`. The request can ask for a step-up but cannot choose what it is; only config feeds those values. The callback then requires a fresh `auth_time`: not in the future (beyond the leeway), not before the sign-in started when `prompt=login` was sent, and within `max_age`, which is 300 seconds when `oidc.step_up.max_age` is not set, so a step-up is never unbounded. In Laravel, `sesame.mfa` with `mfa.on_failure=reauth` sends the user to `/login?step_up=1` for you.

### Identity, roles and claims[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#identity-roles-and-claims)

The username comes from `oidc.username_claim` (default `accessid`, the UPN's prefix). When the token has no such claim, the sign-in fails with `oidc.missing_claim` and the error names the settings to change. `oidc.username_fallback` (off by default) uses the part of `preferred_username` before the `@` instead.

Warning

`preferred_username` can be changed by the user or an admin (a renamed UPN, a guest account), so a fallback username is no stable account key. Turn the fallback on only when the app keys its users on something else (`iss` plus `sub`, or `tid` plus `oid`).

The roles claim (`oidc.roles_claim`, default `wsu_roles`) becomes the `roles` attribute; a mapped claim that arrives under a custom-claim namespace (`http://schemas.example.test/claims/wsu_roles` or `extn.wsu_roles`) is found by its short name. The exact name and the namespaced forms are counted together: two or more candidates (an exact `wsu_roles` beside a namespaced one, say) count as none. `oidc.claims` (default `wsu_roles,accessid`) lists the claims passed to the resolver under their own names, so `$identity->attributes['wsu_roles']` works. Set `roles_claim` (and `claims`) to `wsuRoles` to keep the old name. `iss`, `sub`, `oid`, `tid`, `email`, `name` and `preferred_username` are attributes too; key the app's users on `iss` plus `sub`, or `tid` plus `oid` (S24), never on the username alone.

### MFA[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#mfa)

`auth_time` becomes the identity's MFA time and `amr` its methods, with the cas driver's rules: the driver never invents a sign-in time, and without an MFA method in `amr` the MFA check fails closed. Entra's v2 ID tokens often carry no `amr`; when Conditional Access enforces MFA for this app, `oidc.assume_mfa` adds `mfa` to the methods, exactly like `cas.assume_mfa`. `acrs` (authentication contexts `c1` to `c99`) feeds `hasAuthContext()`.

### Return-to and logout[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#return-to-and-logout)

A login request may carry `return_to`. It is kept only when it passes the ReturnTo rule (an absolute https URL with the redirect URI's scheme, host and port, and no user name or password); anything else is dropped, so it can never be an open redirect. After the callback, `sesame_login()` and the Laravel route send the user there.

The app session is cleared first, as for every driver. With `oidc.post_logout_redirect_uri` set, the user then goes through Entra's `end_session_endpoint` with that `post_logout_redirect_uri`, which must also be registered on the app registration. Without it, logout stays local and the Entra session lives on (the next sign-in is silent).

### Raw PHP[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#raw-php)

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__.'/vendor/autoload.php';

use Nyholm\Psr7\Factory\Psr17Factory;
use Symfony\Component\Cache\Adapter\FilesystemAdapter;
use Symfony\Component\Cache\Psr16Cache;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Config;
use Waynestate\Sesame\DriverFactory;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Sesame;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Session\NativeSession;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Support\Setting;

ini_set('session.gc_maxlifetime', '7200'); // at least SESAME's idle timeout; see Raw PHP
session_start();

$config = Config::fromArray([
    'driver' => 'oidc',
    'environment' => 'production',
    'oidc' => [
        'issuer' => Setting::get('SESAME_OIDC_ISSUER') ?? Setting::get('SESAME_OAUTH2_ISSUER'),
        'client_id' => Setting::get('SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_ID'),
        // client_secret is left out: it is read from SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
        // in the environment, never from the playbook.
        'redirect_uri' => 'https://app.example.test/login.php',
        'post_logout_redirect_uri' => 'https://app.example.test/',
    ],
]);

$session = new NativeSession();
$driver = DriverFactory::make(
    $config,
    new \GuzzleHttp\Client(['allow_redirects' => false, 'timeout' => 10]),
    new Psr17Factory(),
    null,
    null,
    new Psr16Cache(new FilesystemAdapter('sesame')), // optional; without it, discovery and keys are fetched per request
    $session,
);

sesame(new Sesame($driver, new MyUserResolver(), $session, $config));

// login.php: starts the sign-in, finishes it on the callback, then sends the
// user to the checked return_to or back here.
$user = sesame_login();
```

A protected page sends a guest to `login.php?return_to=<its own https URL>`, and a page that needs fresh credentials to `login.php?step_up=1`.

### Laravel[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#laravel)

```
SESAME_DRIVER=oidc
SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=<application (client) id>
SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=<client secret value>
# SESAME_OIDC_ISSUER falls back to SESAME_OAUTH2_ISSUER (and the playbook).
# SESAME_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI defaults to the app's /login/callback route.
SESAME_OIDC_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI=https://app.example.test/
```

The adapter registers `GET /login/callback` (`sesame.callback`) beside `GET /login`, passes the Laravel session and cache to the driver, and after the callback redirects to the checked `return_to`, or to the page `auth.sesame` saved. Laravel's default `SameSite=Lax` session cookie is right: Entra's redirect back is a top-level GET, which Lax allows (S41); `Strict` would drop the cookie and fail every callback with `oidc.state`.

### Config keys[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#config-keys)

| Key | Env | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `oidc.issuer` | `SESAME_OIDC_ISSUER`, then `SESAME_OAUTH2_ISSUER` | none | The issuer, exactly as the discovery document's `issuer`. Required. |
| `oidc.client_id` | `SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` | none | The app registration's client id; the ID token's `aud`. Required. |
| `oidc.client_secret` | `SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | none | Environment only, never the playbook, never logged. Held in a `SensitiveParameterValue`, so `var_export`, `json_encode` and dumps show nothing and `serialize` refuses. Keep PHP's production default `zend.exception_ignore_args = On` as well. Required. |
| `oidc.redirect_uri` | `SESAME_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI` | Laravel: `/login/callback` | Where Entra sends the browser back. https, or `http://localhost` for development. Required in raw PHP. |
| `oidc.scopes` | `SESAME_OIDC_SCOPES` | `openid profile email` | `openid` is always added. |
| `oidc.client_auth` | `SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_AUTH` | `client_secret_post` | Or `client_secret_basic`. |
| `oidc.username_claim` | `SESAME_OIDC_USERNAME_CLAIM` | `accessid` | The claim the username comes from. |
| `oidc.username_fallback` | `SESAME_OIDC_USERNAME_FALLBACK` | `false` | Opt in to the `preferred_username` prefix when the claim is missing. `preferred_username` is user-changeable; see the warning above. |
| `oidc.roles_claim` | `SESAME_OIDC_ROLES_CLAIM` | `wsu_roles` | The claim that becomes the `roles` attribute; namespaced forms are found. |
| `oidc.claims` | `SESAME_OIDC_CLAIMS` | `wsu_roles,accessid` | Claims passed to the resolver as attributes under their own names. |
| `oidc.assume_mfa` | `SESAME_OIDC_ASSUME_MFA` | `false` | Count a sign-in as MFA when Conditional Access enforces it for the app. |
| `oidc.algorithms` | none | `['RS256']` | The ID token algorithms allowed: `RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512` only. |
| `oidc.leeway_seconds` | `SESAME_OIDC_LEEWAY_SECONDS` | `60` | Clock skew on `exp`, `nbf` and `iat`, at most 300. |
| `oidc.post_logout_redirect_uri` | `SESAME_OIDC_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI` | none | Set it to log out of Entra too. |
| `oidc.authorization_endpoint`, `oidc.token_endpoint`, `oidc.jwks_uri`, `oidc.end_session_endpoint` | `SESAME_OIDC_AUTHORIZATION_ENDPOINT` and so on | discovered | Overrides; with the first three set, discovery is skipped. |
| `oidc.cache_ttl_seconds` | `SESAME_OIDC_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` | `3600` | How long the discovery document and key set are kept, 1 to 3600 seconds (at most an hour, so a moved endpoint or revoked key does not live on). |
| `oidc.cache_store` | `SESAME_OIDC_CACHE_STORE` | the default store | Laravel only. |
| `oidc.state_ttl_seconds` | none | `600` | How long a started sign-in may take, 60 to 3600 seconds. |
| `oidc.step_up.prompt` | `SESAME_OIDC_STEP_UP_PROMPT` | `login` | Sent on a step-up only; `login` or empty. |
| `oidc.step_up.max_age` | `SESAME_OIDC_STEP_UP_MAX_AGE` | none (300 enforced) | Seconds; sent on a step-up only, and enforced on `auth_time`. Unset, it is not sent, but a step-up `auth_time` older than 300 seconds still fails. |
| `oidc.step_up.acr_values` | `SESAME_OIDC_STEP_UP_ACR_VALUES` | none | Sent on a step-up only. |
| `oidc.step_up.claims` | `SESAME_OIDC_STEP_UP_CLAIMS` | none | A JSON object (for example an `acrs` request for an Entra authentication context), sent on a step-up only. |

Danger

`SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` is environment only: never the playbook, never logged. It is held in a `SensitiveParameterValue`, so `var_export`, `json_encode` and dumps show nothing and `serialize` refuses. Keep PHP's production default `zend.exception_ignore_args = On` as well.

### The Entra app registration[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#the-entra-app-registration)

What the developer (or the Entra admin) sets on the app registration:

- **Platform: Web**, with the redirect URI exactly as `oidc.redirect_uri` (for Laravel, `https://<app host>/login/callback`). Add `http://localhost:<port>/login/callback` only on a development registration.
- **Post-logout redirect**: when you set `oidc.post_logout_redirect_uri`, register that address as a redirect URI too.
- **Certificates and secrets**: a client secret, stored only in the app's environment (`SESAME_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`); rotate it before it expires.
- **Authentication**: leave the implicit grant's "ID tokens" and "Access tokens" boxes unchecked; the code flow does not need them.
- **Token configuration**: add the optional ID token claim `auth_time` (and `email` if the app wants it). Ask the Entra admin for the mapped `wsu_roles` and `accessid` claims (a claims-mapping policy); if they arrive under a namespace, SESAME finds them by their short names.
- **Enterprise application, Properties: Assignment required = Yes**, then assign the groups that may sign in. This is what limits an app to, for example, employees only: Entra refuses everyone else before SESAME sees them. Check roles in the app as well (S25).
- **API permissions**: `openid`, `profile` and `email` (Microsoft Graph, delegated) are enough.

Use the v2.0 issuer (`https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0`); the tenant id comes from the playbook or the environment, never from code.

### Related[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html#related)

- [Which driver for my app?](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/which-driver.html)
- [The gateway driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-gateway.html)
- [The cas driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html)
- [oauth2 with Entra](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oauth2-entra.html)
- [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [Laravel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)
- [Requiring MFA](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/requiring-mfa.html)
- [Step-up (authentication context)](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/step-up.html)

## The saml driver (SAML 2.0 sign-in)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#the-saml-driver-saml-2-0-sign-in)

The goal: sign a person into your app through the browser with SAML 2.0, with your app as the service provider (SP) and a Shibboleth-style identity provider (IdP) vouching for them. This page walks through how a sign-in runs, every config key, and what to hand the IdP's administrators; then set the driver up on the [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html) or [Laravel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html) page.

Note

The saml driver is opt-in. Nothing in it runs unless `SESAME_DRIVER=saml`, and SESAME assumes no IdP: there is no default WSU IdP entity, so you name the IdP's metadata yourself. On Citadel prefer the `gateway` driver behind Drawbridge, and for Entra prefer `oidc`. Reach for SAML when the IdP you must use speaks only SAML.

### What you need[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#what-you-need)

Open sesame, in a language with a schema. The saml driver stands on `onelogin/php-saml`, which SESAME suggests but does not require:

```
composer require onelogin/php-saml
```

Without it, building the driver fails with `The saml driver needs onelogin/php-saml. Install it with: composer require onelogin/php-saml`. With a release older than the floor (php-saml 4.3.2, xmlseclibs 3.1.5, both for published signature and encryption advisories), building the driver fails too, and SESAME's `composer.json` refuses to install those releases beside it. Why that library, and what else was weighed: [docs/saml-library-choice.md](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html).

You also need:

- The IdP's metadata: an https URL, or the XML saved as a file in the deploy. Exactly one.
- A shared PSR-16 cache (in Laravel, a cache store every web server sees). The driver parks the IdP's answer there for two minutes, keeps the fetched metadata, and remembers the assertion IDs it has accepted.
- The app's session (SESAME's `SessionPort`), as for `cas` and `oidc`.
- Optionally an SP key pair, as file paths, for signed AuthnRequests and the certificate in the SP metadata.

### How a sign-in runs[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#how-a-sign-in-runs)

A SAML sign-in takes three requests, one more than you might expect.

1. **The start.** A request to the login URL without `saml_handle` builds an AuthnRequest (the HTTP-Redirect binding, signed when `saml.sign_authn_requests` is on), keeps its ID in the app's session (bound to this browser, single use, gone after ten minutes), and redirects to the IdP. A checked `return_to` rides along as the RelayState.
2. **The ACS.** The IdP posts its Response to the ACS URL. That POST is cross-site, so the browser sends no `SameSite=Lax` session cookie with it (S35, S41), and a session started there would replace the user's real one. So the ACS never touches the session: it parks the raw, unchecked Response in the PSR-16 cache under a random 256-bit handle (single use, two minutes) and answers `303 See Other` to the login URL with `saml_handle=<handle>`.
3. **The finish.** That GET is a top-level navigation, so the session cookie is back. The driver takes the parked Response and the pending request it answers (both single use), and php-saml validates it in strict mode: the XML schema (no DOCTYPE), the signature and exactly what it covers, Destination and Recipient against the configured ACS URL, Audience against the SP entity ID, Issuer against the IdP, InResponseTo against the pending request, the time conditions, and the bearer subject confirmation. SESAME then adds its own checks: a signed assertion (always), SHA-2 signatures and digests only, an IssueInstant no further ahead than `saml.leeway_seconds` and no older than `saml.max_assertion_age_seconds`, and an assertion ID the replay guard has never seen. The identity goes to the app's `findOrImportUser(Identity)`, and the core regenerates the session ID, as for every driver.

`sesame_login()` and the Laravel route then send the user to the checked return-to, so the handle never stays in the address bar.

IdP-initiated (unsolicited) responses are refused: a sign-in must start at the app. A Response that answers another browser's request (login CSRF) is refused too, because the pending request lives in this browser's session.

### Identity, attributes and MFA[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#identity-attributes-and-mfa)

`saml.attributes` maps SESAME's names to the SAML attribute names the IdP releases; the first name present wins. The defaults are the eduPerson and inetOrgPerson OIDs a Shibboleth IdP releases, then their friendly names:

| SESAME name | SAML attribute names (default) |
| --- | --- |
| `accessid` | `urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.1`, `uid` |
| `email` | `urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3`, `mail` |
| `name` | `urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113730.3.1.241`, `displayName` |
| `affiliations` | `urn:oid:1.3.6.1.4.1.5923.1.1.1.1`, `eduPersonAffiliation` |
| `eppn` | `urn:oid:1.3.6.1.4.1.5923.1.1.1.6`, `eduPersonPrincipalName` |

The username comes from `saml.username_attribute` (default `accessid`). When the assertion has no such attribute, the sign-in fails with `saml.missing_attribute` and the error names the settings to change. The mapped attributes reach the resolver under SESAME's names (`$identity->attributes['affiliations']`), along with `issuer`, `name_id` (when the IdP sends one) and `authn_context`.

The AuthnStatement gives the MFA facts. `AuthnInstant` becomes the identity's sign-in time (never invented: without one, the MFA check fails closed). An `AuthnContextClassRef` listed in `saml.mfa_contexts` (the REFEDS MFA profile, `https://refeds.org/profile/mfa`, by default) adds `mfa` to the methods, and the class reference is also the identity's authentication context, so `sesame.context:https://refeds.org/profile/mfa` works. `saml.assume_mfa` counts every sign-in as MFA, for an IdP that enforces MFA for this SP but does not say so.

### Step-up and return-to[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#step-up-and-return-to)

A login request with `step_up=1` sends `ForceAuthn="true"`, so the IdP asks for credentials again. The finish then requires a fresh `AuthnInstant`: not in the future beyond the leeway, not before the sign-in started, and within 300 seconds. In Laravel, `sesame.mfa` with `mfa.on_failure=reauth` sends the user to `/login?step_up=1` for you.

A login request may carry `return_to`. It goes out as the RelayState only when it passes the ReturnTo rule (an absolute https URL with the login URL's scheme, host and port, and no user name or password), and the RelayState that comes back is checked again with the same rule, so it can never be an open redirect.

### Logout[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#logout)

Local only. There is no single logout: SESAME refuses `slo` at boot, so the app session is cleared and the IdP's session lives on (the next sign-in is usually silent).

### Raw PHP[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#raw-php)

The ACS is its own page, and it must NOT call `session_start()`.

```php
<?php
// boot-saml.php: shared by the three pages below. No session_start() here.

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__.'/vendor/autoload.php';

use Nyholm\Psr7\Factory\Psr17Factory;
use Symfony\Component\Cache\Adapter\FilesystemAdapter;
use Symfony\Component\Cache\Psr16Cache;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Config;
use Waynestate\Sesame\DriverFactory;
use Waynestate\Sesame\Session\NativeSession;

$config = Config::fromArray([
    'driver' => 'saml',
    'environment' => 'production',
    'saml' => [
        'sp' => [
            'entity_id' => 'https://app.example.test/metadata.php',
            'acs_url' => 'https://app.example.test/acs.php',
            'cert_file' => getenv('SESAME_SAML_SP_CERT_FILE') ?: null,
            'key_file' => getenv('SESAME_SAML_SP_KEY_FILE') ?: null,
        ],
        'idp' => [
            'metadata_file' => __DIR__.'/config/idp-metadata.xml',
        ],
        'service_url' => 'https://app.example.test/login.php',
    ],
]);

$session = new NativeSession(); // does not start the session
$driver = DriverFactory::make(
    $config,
    new \GuzzleHttp\Client(['allow_redirects' => false, 'timeout' => 10]), // only for a metadata URL
    new Psr17Factory(),
    null,
    null,
    new Psr16Cache(new FilesystemAdapter('sesame')), // shared by every web server
    $session,
);
```

```php
<?php
// acs.php: the IdP posts here. No session_start(): the 303 goes to login.php.
require __DIR__.'/boot-saml.php';
sesame_saml_acs($driver);
```

```php
<?php
// metadata.php: the SP metadata for the IdP's administrators.
require __DIR__.'/boot-saml.php';
sesame_saml_metadata($driver);
```

```php
<?php
// login.php: starts the sign-in, finishes it with the saml_handle, then
// sends the user to the checked return_to or back here.
require __DIR__.'/boot-saml.php';

use Waynestate\Sesame\Sesame;

ini_set('session.gc_maxlifetime', '7200'); // at least SESAME's idle timeout; see Raw PHP
session_start();

sesame(new Sesame($driver, new MyUserResolver(), $session, $config));

$user = sesame_login();
```

A protected page sends a guest to `login.php?return_to=<its own https URL>`, and a page that needs fresh credentials to `login.php?step_up=1`.

### Laravel[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#laravel)

```
SESAME_DRIVER=saml
SESAME_SAML_IDP_METADATA_URL=<the IdP's metadata URL>
# or SESAME_SAML_IDP_METADATA_FILE=/path/to/idp-metadata.xml
# The SP entity ID, the ACS URL and the login URL default to the app's
# /login/saml/metadata, /login/saml/acs and /login routes.
SESAME_SAML_SP_CERT_FILE=/path/to/sp.crt
SESAME_SAML_SP_KEY_FILE=/path/to/sp.key
SESAME_SAML_CACHE_STORE=redis
```

The adapter registers two more routes beside `GET /login`, both outside the `web` middleware group, because neither may start a session:

| Route | Name | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /login/saml/acs` | `sesame.saml.acs` | Parks the IdP's Response and answers 303 to `/login?saml_handle=...`; an unusable POST gets a plain 400. No session, no CSRF token (the IdP cannot send one). |
| `GET /login/saml/metadata` | `sesame.saml.metadata` | The SP metadata as `application/samlmetadata+xml`. |

It passes the Laravel session and the `sesame.saml.cache_store` cache to the driver. Laravel's default `SameSite=Lax` session cookie is right: the browser drops it on the IdP's POST, which is why the ACS parks the response, and sends it on the 303's GET. `Strict` would drop it on that GET too.

### What to hand the IdP's administrators[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#what-to-hand-the-idp-s-administrators)

Send them the SP metadata URL (`/login/saml/metadata` in Laravel). It carries the entity ID, the ACS URL with the HTTP-POST binding, `WantAssertionsSigned="true"` and, when set, the SP certificate. Ask them:

- to **sign assertions** (Shibboleth's `signAssertions` for this SP). SESAME refuses an unsigned assertion even inside a signed Response;
- to release the attributes in `saml.attributes` (by default the AccessID as `uid`, plus `mail`, `displayName` and `eduPersonAffiliation`);
- to sign with SHA-256 or better; SHA-1 is refused;
- not to encrypt assertions unless the app has an SP key pair to decrypt them with.

### Config keys[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#config-keys)

| Key | Env | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `saml.sp.entity_id` | `SESAME_SAML_SP_ENTITY_ID` | Laravel: `/login/saml/metadata` | The SP's entity ID, as the IdP knows the app. Required in raw PHP. |
| `saml.sp.acs_url` | `SESAME_SAML_SP_ACS_URL` | Laravel: `/login/saml/acs` | Where the IdP posts its Response. https, or `http://localhost` for development. Required in raw PHP. |
| `saml.service_url` | `SESAME_SAML_SERVICE_URL` | Laravel: `/login` | The login URL, where a sign-in starts and finishes; every return-to must stay on its host. Required in raw PHP. |
| `saml.sp.cert_file`, `saml.sp.key_file` | `SESAME_SAML_SP_CERT_FILE`, `SESAME_SAML_SP_KEY_FILE` | none | The SP's PEM certificate and private key, as file paths; set both or neither. The key must match the certificate. Never inline, never logged: the key is held in a `SensitiveParameterValue`. |
| `saml.sign_authn_requests` | `SESAME_SAML_SIGN_AUTHN_REQUESTS` | `false` | Sign the AuthnRequest (RSA-SHA256). Needs the SP key pair. |
| `saml.want_messages_signed` | `SESAME_SAML_WANT_MESSAGES_SIGNED` | `false` | Also require a signed Response. The assertion signature is required either way. |
| `saml.idp.metadata_url` | `SESAME_SAML_IDP_METADATA_URL` | none | The IdP's metadata, https only, fetched without following redirects and cached. Set this or the file. |
| `saml.idp.metadata_file` | `SESAME_SAML_IDP_METADATA_FILE` | none | The IdP's metadata XML as a file, read at boot (a bad file stops the app). Set this or the URL. |
| `saml.idp.entity_id` | `SESAME_SAML_IDP_ENTITY_ID` | none | Which IdP in the metadata to trust; required when the document holds more than one. No default WSU IdP. |
| `saml.idp.cert_file` | `SESAME_SAML_IDP_CERT_FILE` | the metadata's signing certificates | Pin the IdP's signing certificate. |
| `saml.attributes` | `SESAME_SAML_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESSID`, `_EMAIL`, `_NAME`, `_AFFILIATIONS`, `_EPPN` | the table above | SESAME's name to SAML attribute names, comma-separated; an empty value keeps the default for that name. |
| `saml.username_attribute` | `SESAME_SAML_USERNAME_ATTRIBUTE` | `accessid` | Which mapped attribute becomes the username. |
| `saml.mfa_contexts` | `SESAME_SAML_MFA_CONTEXTS` | `https://refeds.org/profile/mfa` | AuthnContextClassRef values that count as MFA. |
| `saml.assume_mfa` | `SESAME_SAML_ASSUME_MFA` | `false` | Count every sign-in as MFA, when the IdP enforces it for this SP. |
| `saml.authn_context` | `SESAME_SAML_AUTHN_CONTEXT` | none | AuthnContextClassRef values to request (a RequestedAuthnContext); none is sent by default. |
| `saml.leeway_seconds` | `SESAME_SAML_LEEWAY_SECONDS` | `60` | Clock skew on the IssueInstant and the step-up checks, 0 to 180 seconds. php-saml's own conditions allow a fixed 180. |
| `saml.max_assertion_age_seconds` | `SESAME_SAML_MAX_ASSERTION_AGE_SECONDS` | `300` | The oldest an assertion may be, by its IssueInstant, 30 to 3600 seconds. |
| `saml.metadata_cache_ttl_seconds` | `SESAME_SAML_METADATA_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` | `3600` | How long fetched metadata is kept, 60 to 86400 seconds. |
| `saml.request_ttl_seconds` | none | `600` | How long a started sign-in may take, 60 to 3600 seconds. |
| `saml.cache_store` | `SESAME_SAML_CACHE_STORE` | the default store | Laravel only. Must be shared by every web server of the app. |

### Errors[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html#errors)

Every refusal is an `AuthenticationFailed` with a short reason in parentheses, never a value from the XML:

| Reason | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| `saml.acs` | The ACS got no usable `SAMLResponse` (not a POST, empty, too large, not base64). |
| `saml.handle` | The `saml_handle` is unknown, used, or older than two minutes. |
| `saml.response` | The Response is not well-formed XML, or carries a DOCTYPE. |
| `saml.unsolicited` | The Response answers no request (IdP-initiated). |
| `saml.in_response_to` | It answers a request this browser did not send, or one already used or expired. |
| `saml.invalid: <code>` | php-saml refused it; the code is its `ValidationError` name, for example `no_signed_assertion`, `invalid_signature`, `wrong_audience`, `wrong_issuer`, `wrong_destination`, `assertion_expired` or `wrong_number_of_assertions`. |
| `saml.algorithm` | A signature or digest outside SHA-2. |
| `saml.issue_instant`, `saml.too_old` | The IssueInstant is in the future beyond the leeway, or older than the maximum age. |
| `saml.replay` | The assertion ID was accepted before. |
| `saml.step_up` | A step-up sign-in was not fresh. |
| `saml.missing_attribute` | The username attribute is missing. |
| `saml.metadata` | The IdP metadata could not be fetched or used. |

## Laravel[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#laravel)

The Laravel adapter is a service provider that binds the core into the container, registers the `auth.sesame` and `wayne.cas` middleware aliases, and, unless the app has taken the routes over, registers the login and logout routes. It holds no rules of its own: every rule lives in the core. This page is how to wire it into an app and read the signed-in user back; next, see [Requiring MFA](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/requiring-mfa.html) and [Step-up (authentication context)](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/step-up.html) for the checks the middleware runs.

### Install and publish[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#install-and-publish)

The provider is discovered automatically. Publish the config with:

```
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=sesame-config
```

The app's environment becomes the core's `environment`, the `cas.service_url` falls back to the app's `/login` route when the app has not set one, and the oidc driver's `redirect_uri` falls back to the app's `/login/callback` route. For the saml driver, `saml.service_url`, `saml.sp.acs_url` and `saml.sp.entity_id` fall back to the app's `/login`, `/login/saml/acs` and `/login/saml/metadata` routes.

### Config[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#config)

Config keys (in `config/sesame.php`):

| Key | Env | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `driver` | `SESAME_DRIVER` | `cas` | `cas`, `gateway`, `oauth2`, `oidc`, `saml` or `fake`. The oidc keys are in [The oidc driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-oidc.html), the saml keys in [The saml driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-saml.html). |
| `cas.base_url` | `SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL` | none | The CAS server, an absolute https:// URL. |
| `cas.service_url` | `SESAME_CAS_SERVICE_URL` | the app's `/login` route | Where the server sends the user back to. |
| `cas.protocol` | `SESAME_CAS_PROTOCOL` | `2.0` | `3.0` or `2.0`. |
| `cas.assume_mfa` | `SESAME_CAS_ASSUME_MFA` | `false` | A successful validation counts as an MFA sign-in. On only when the CAS server enforces MFA for every sign-in. |
| `fake.username` | `SESAME_FAKE_USERNAME` | none | The fake driver's username. |
| `gateway.header` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_HEADER` | `X-Sesame-Assertion` | The one header that holds the signed assertion. |
| `gateway.algorithm` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_ALGORITHM` | `ES256` | `ES256`, `RS256` or `EdDSA`. |
| `gateway.public_key` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_PUBLIC_KEY` | none | The gateway's public key. Required for the gateway driver. |
| `gateway.issuer` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_ISSUER` | none | The `iss` claim the assertion must carry. Required for the gateway driver. |
| `gateway.audience` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_AUDIENCE` | none | The `aud` claim the assertion must carry. Required for the gateway driver. |
| `gateway.leeway_seconds` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_LEEWAY_SECONDS` | `30` | Clock skew allowed on the time-claim checks, in seconds. |
| `gateway.trusted_proxies` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | none | Comma-separated CIDR ranges (or single IPs) the gateway proxy sits behind. Required for the gateway driver. |
| `gateway.max_lifetime` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_MAX_LIFETIME` | `300` | The longest an assertion may live, in seconds. |
| `gateway.replay_store` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_REPLAY_STORE` | the app's default cache store | The cache store the used `jti`s are kept in (Laravel only). |
| `gateway.allow_without_replay_guard` | `SESAME_GATEWAY_ALLOW_WITHOUT_REPLAY_GUARD` | `false` | Skip the replay guard. Local development only. |
| `oauth2.issuer` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_ISSUER` | none | The `iss` claim the token must carry. Required for the oauth2 driver. |
| `oauth2.jwks_url` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_JWKS_URL` | none | The URL of the issuer's key set. Required for the oauth2 driver. |
| `oauth2.audience` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_AUDIENCE` | none | The `aud` claim the token must carry. Required for the oauth2 driver. |
| `oauth2.leeway_seconds` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_LEEWAY_SECONDS` | `60` | Clock skew allowed on the time-claim checks, in seconds. |
| `oauth2.identity_claim` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_IDENTITY_CLAIM` | `preferred_username` | The claim the username comes from: `preferred_username` or `accessid`. |
| `oauth2.jwks_cache_ttl_seconds` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_JWKS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` | `3600` | How long the fetched key set is kept, in seconds. |
| `oauth2.jwks_store` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_JWKS_STORE` | the app's default cache store | The cache store the key set is kept in (Laravel only). |
| `oauth2.require_at_jwt` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_REQUIRE_AT_JWT` | `false` | Refuse a token whose `typ` header is not `at+jwt` (RFC 9068). Leave it off for Entra. |
| `oauth2.introspection_url` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_URL` | none | The RFC 7662 endpoint for opaque bearer tokens. Leave it unset to keep the driver JWT-only. |
| `oauth2.introspection_client_id` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_ID` | none | The client id sent as HTTP Basic auth to the introspection endpoint. Required when the URL is set. |
| `oauth2.introspection_client_secret` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_SECRET` | none | The client secret sent as HTTP Basic auth to the introspection endpoint. Required when the URL is set. |
| `oauth2.introspection_cache_ttl_seconds` | `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` | `60` | How long an accepted introspection answer is kept, in seconds, capped by the token's `exp`. Zero disables the cache. |
| `session.idle_minutes` | `SESAME_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES` | `120` | Drop the session after this much quiet time, in minutes. |
| `session.absolute_minutes` | `SESAME_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MINUTES` | `720` | End the session this long after sign-in, in minutes. |
| `mfa.max_age` | `SESAME_MFA_MAX_AGE` | `28800` | The longest a user's last MFA sign-in may be, in seconds. |
| `mfa.on_failure` | `SESAME_MFA_ON_FAILURE` | `deny` | `deny` answers a 403; `reauth` redirects to the login route. |
| `routes` | `SESAME_ROUTES` | `true` | Register the login and logout routes. |
| `log` | `SESAME_LOG` | `true` | Log the sign-in and sign-out events through the app's PSR-3 logger. Set to `false` to turn them off. |
| `user_resolver` | `SESAME_USER_RESOLVER` | none | The class that resolves a verified identity to the app's user. Required. |

A missing `user_resolver` fails with an error that names the wayne-cas resolver class. The driver is built lazily: resolving SESAME does not build it, so guests on http, artisan commands, queue workers and tests can ask who is signed in; the driver (and its https check) is built when someone signs in or out, and an app with a broken config still boots and answers signed-out requests.

### Routes[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#routes)

The routes, when `routes` is true:

| Method | Path | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/login` | `sesame.login` |
| `POST` | `/logout` | `sesame.logout` (in the `web` group, so Laravel's CSRF check applies; a form needs `@csrf`) |
| `GET` | `/login/callback` | `sesame.callback` (oidc driver only) |
| `POST` | `/login/saml/acs` | `sesame.saml.acs` (saml driver only; outside the `web` group, so no session and no CSRF token: the IdP's POST cannot carry either) |
| `GET` | `/login/saml/metadata` | `sesame.saml.metadata` (saml driver only; the SP metadata) |

Set `SESAME_ROUTES=false` when the app defines its own login and logout routes. The `auth.sesame` middleware still points at the `sesame.login` route name, so the app's login route must keep that name.

### Middleware[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#middleware)

Protect a route with the `auth.sesame` middleware:

```php
Route::get('/dashboard', fn () => view('dashboard'))->middleware('auth.sesame');
```

A guest is sent to the login route; a JSON guest gets a 401.

Require MFA on a route with the `sesame.mfa` middleware:

```php
Route::get('/vault', fn () => view('vault'))->middleware(['auth.sesame', 'sesame.mfa']);
```

It lets the request through when the signed-in user's MFA is still good, and otherwise stops it: a 403 by default, a JSON 403 for JSON requests, and a redirect to the login route when `mfa.on_failure` is `reauth`. The allowed age comes from the route parameter when there is one, and from `mfa.max_age` when there is not:

```php
Route::get('/vault', fn () => view('vault'))->middleware(['auth.sesame', 'sesame.mfa:3600']);
```

The `sesame.context` middleware does the step-up context check on a route:

```php
Route::get('/vault', [VaultController::class, 'index'])
    ->middleware(['web', 'auth.sesame', 'sesame.context:c1']);
```

A request without the context gets a 403, or a JSON 403 with a `message` for JSON requests. A route that names no context fails closed. See [Step-up (authentication context)](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/step-up.html).

The `wayne.cas` alias is registered against SESAME's `WayneAuthenticate`, for apps moving off wayne-cas; see [Moving from wayne-cas](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html).

### Reading the user[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#reading-the-user)

The app's user is available through the facade:

```php
$user = app(\Waynestate\Sesame\Sesame::class)->user();
```

SESAME stores the user your resolver returned at sign-in and hands back that same copy until the session ends. When the app wants the signed-in user read back from its own store on every request, so a change made after the sign-in (a removed role, a deleted account) shows up from the next request on, the resolver also implements `Waynestate\Sesame\RefreshesUser`: its `refreshUser($user)` runs on every request, and a `null` answer signs the session out. The wayne-cas shim already implements it, looking the user up through `auth.providers.users.model`; a resolver that does not implement it keeps handing back the stored copy, as it always has.

On Laravel 13, implement it. Laravel 13 stores sessions as JSON, so the user SESAME saved at sign-in comes back on the next request as a plain array instead of the app's User model, and the guard sees nobody. `refreshUser()` receives that array (or the model itself when the session is still PHP-serialized) and must return the app's User: look it up by a stable key such as the username or the primary key, and return `null` when the user is gone, which signs the session out. Sourdough's Laravel templates already ship this:

```php
public function refreshUser(mixed $user): mixed
{
    $username = match (true) {
        $user instanceof User => $user->username,
        is_array($user) => $user['username'] ?? null,
        default => null,
    };

    if (! is_string($username) || $username === '') {
        return null;
    }

    return User::where('username', $username)->first();
}
```

The same user is available through Laravel's own auth, because the provider registers a `sesame` guard driver. Point a guard in `config/auth.php` at it:

```php
'guards' => [
    'web' => [
        'driver' => 'sesame',
        'provider' => 'users',
    ],
],
```

and the usual calls work against the SESAME session: `auth()->user()`, `$request->user()`, `Auth::check()`, and the `auth` middleware. The note above applies here too: the guard hands back the stored copy, or the refreshed one when the resolver refreshes. A user that is not an `Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable` reads as `null` through the guard; the `auth.sesame` middleware still sees it, because it checks the SESAME session directly.

`auth()->logout()` signs the user out of both sides, the Laravel session and the SESAME session. The identity provider's single sign-on session is left alone.

### HTTP client and caches[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#http-client-and-caches)

The cas and oauth2 drivers need a PSR-18 client. The adapter uses the app's `Psr\Http\Client\ClientInterface` binding when there is one, Guzzle when it is installed (with redirects off), and nothing when there is neither. Bind a client when the app has neither:

```php
app()->singleton(
    Psr\Http\Client\ClientInterface::class,
    fn () => new \Symfony\Component\HttpClient\Psr18Client(),
);
```

The oauth2 driver also keeps its fetched key set in a PSR-16 cache. The adapter wires one up from the app's cache, using the store named by `oauth2.jwks_store`, or the default store when none is named. The gateway driver's replay guard is wired the same way, from the store named by `gateway.replay_store`, so a captured assertion cannot be played back a second time.

### Logging[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#logging)

The adapter passes the app's PSR-3 logger to the core, so a Laravel app gets the authentication events in its normal log channels with no extra wiring: the container's `Psr\Log\LoggerInterface` binding is used when there is one. Set `sesame.log` (env `SESAME_LOG`) to `false` to turn the events off; the default is `true`. The events, their context and what is never logged are described in [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html), "Logging".

### Related[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)
- [Which driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/which-driver.html)
- [Requiring MFA](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/requiring-mfa.html)
- [Step-up (authentication context)](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/step-up.html)
- [Session timeouts](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session-timeouts.html)
- [Moving from wayne-cas](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html)

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html

## Moving from wayne-cas[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#moving-from-wayne-cas)

Apps that use wayne-cas can move to SESAME without rewriting their auth. Open sesame, indeed: the same door, a new lock. The easy way is Booster's `cas-to-sesame` hop; the by-hand path is below it.

Note

Still on the older Wayne Auth SSO cookie (`new WayneAuth(...)`, `authenticateSSO()`) rather than wayne-cas? See [Moving off Wayne Auth](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html): a bridge keeps those calls and moves the sign-in to CAS with a one-line change.

### The easy way: Booster's `cas-to-sesame` hop[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#the-easy-way-booster-s-cas-to-sesame-hop)

Booster plans the hop with `--sesame`, and leaves it out with a warning when the plan ends below PHP 8.3, which SESAME needs. It lands just before the hop from Laravel 10 to 11, and while PHP is still below 8.3 the PHP hops go first. What the hop does:

- Writes `config/sesame.php` from the app's `config/wayne-cas.php` when the old `root` is a plain string (the old root becomes the fallback for `cas.base_url`), or from SESAME's published defaults when the app has no wayne-cas config at all. `user_resolver` defaults to the compat resolver.
- Moves the CAS middleware off the global `web` group and onto the app's web routes, with the `wayne.cas` alias registered against SESAME's `WayneAuthenticate`.
- Points the web guard at the `sesame` driver and the users provider at `eloquent`, adding a model key when the provider has none.
- Rewrites user models that use `WayneCasable` as a trait to `implements WayneCasable` plus `use ReadOnlyAttributes`.
- Swaps the Composer requirement to `waynestate/sesame:^0.6` (SESAME is on Packagist, so no extra repository is needed; Booster 1.12.0 and later write `^0.6`, and an app hopped by an earlier Booster got `^0.4`, so take the [0.5.0 and 0.6.0 steps](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html)) and drops the `wayne-cas` package, any `wayne-cas` path entry and its VCS repository entries.
- Removes `config/wayne-cas.php` when nothing in the app reads its config keys any more; while anything still does, the file stays and a manual note names the readers.
- Flags the dead `DUO_*` settings in example env files.

Note

It never runs app code: the old files are read with conservative patterns, and anything it cannot move safely comes back as a manual note that names the file.

### By hand[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#by-hand)

Warning

The shim keeps the wayne-cas names and behavior, and it says once (in the log) that it is a deprecated bridge.

#### The mapping[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#the-mapping)

The mapping:

| wayne-cas | SESAME |
| --- | --- |
| `wayne-cas.root` | `sesame.cas.base_url` |
| `auth.providers.users.model` | `auth.providers.users.model` (unchanged) |
| `WayneCasable` trait | `implements WayneCasable` + `use ReadOnlyAttributes` |
| `WayneAuthenticate` middleware | the `wayne.cas` middleware alias |
| `auth()->user()` through the `wayneCas` guard | `auth()->user()` with the guard pointed at `sesame`, or `app(Sesame::class)->user()` |
| `use2FA` | not supported; the shim logs a warning when it is on |

#### The model[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#the-model)

The model. wayne-cas found the user through the model's static `findOrImportUser`, with the verified username as the access ID. The shim keeps that, and the model keeps its wayne-cas shape:

```php
class User extends Model implements WayneCasable
{
    use Notifiable, ReadOnlyAttributes;

    public static function findOrImportUser($accessId)
    {
        return static::firstOrCreate(['username' => $accessId]);
    }

    public function getReadOnlyAttributes($persistedAttributes = []): array
    {
        return [
            'cn' => $persistedAttributes['cn'] ?? null,
        ];
    }
}
```

The one change a wayne-cas model needs: `getReadOnlyAttributes` goes from protected to public, keeping its `$persistedAttributes` parameter. The interface and the trait share that signature, so a model that satisfies one satisfies both.

The `WayneCasable` interface and the `ReadOnlyAttributes` trait are in the `Waynestate\Sesame\WayneCas` namespace.

#### The middleware[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#the-middleware)

The middleware. wayne-cas's `WayneAuthenticate` middleware is kept as the `wayne.cas` alias. It checks the SESAME session instead of the Laravel auth guard, and it sends unauthenticated users to the `sesame.login` route. The AJAX 403 is kept, because wayne-cas returned it. It is safe in the global `web` group (it lets the `sesame.login`, `sesame.callback` and `sesame.logout` routes straight through), though putting it on the app's routes is still the recommended setup; an app that takes the routes over with `sesame.routes = false` must keep those names or exclude its routes.

#### The guard[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#the-guard)

The guard. wayne-cas apps that read the user through `auth()->user()` can keep that call: point the app's guard at the `sesame` driver (see [Laravel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)) and `auth()->user()`, `Auth::check()` and `auth()->logout()` all work against the SESAME session. Without the guard, the equivalent is `app(Sesame::class)->user()`.

#### The service URL[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#the-service-url)

The service URL. wayne-cas built the service URL from the current request. SESAME takes `sesame.cas.service_url` from config; the Laravel adapter defaults it to the app's `/login` route when it is not set.

#### `use2FA` [#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#use2fa)

`use2FA`. wayne-cas's `use2FA` runs a Duo challenge the shim does not carry. When the app still has `wayne-cas.use2FA` switched on, the shim logs a warning once and leaves the 2FA to the app.

### What Booster leaves for you[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#what-booster-leaves-for-you)

- Duo 2FA is not carried. If the app had `use2FA` enabled, re-enable two-factor in the app itself, and drop the `DUO_HOSTNAME`, `DUO_IKEY`, `DUO_SKEY` and `DUO_AKEY` settings: they do nothing under SESAME.
- Log in through the pre-production host before you ship, and check the session timeout, the Access ID attribute and Duo there.
- `auth()->user()` now comes from SESAME's guard and is reloaded every request (the compat resolver looks the user up again through `auth.providers.users.model`), so check that signed-in pages and any Gate or policy checks still work.

### Related[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html#related)

- [Laravel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html)
- [Which driver for my app?](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/which-driver.html)
- [The cas driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html)
- [Running off Citadel](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.html)
- [Moving off Wayne Auth](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html)

---

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html

## Moving off Wayne Auth[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#moving-off-wayne-auth)

Older WSU PHP apps sign people in through **Wayne Auth**: a small PHP class reads the SSO cookie and checks it with the Wayne Auth service over a socket. Wayne Auth is deprecated. When the service is retired, every app still calling it stops letting anyone in, whatever PHP version it runs. SESAME's Wayne Auth bridge turns that move into a one-line change: the app keeps its `new WayneAuth(...)`, `authenticateSSO()` and `getAccessID()` calls, and they sign people in through CAS instead. Open sesame, say the magic words you already know.

Warning

The bridge is deprecated on arrival. It exists so the move off Wayne Auth is small and provable today; plan the move to SESAME's native calls next (the last section). It says so once per process, as a silenced `E_USER_DEPRECATED` that reaches your error log but never the page.

### Does this fit my app?[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#does-this-fit-my-app)

The bridge keeps the API of the classic `WayneAuth` class, the one apps copy into `lib/` or next to their pages:

```php
$wayne_auth = new WayneAuth($config['wayneauth']);
if ($wayne_auth->authenticateSSO() == true) {
    $accessid = $wayne_auth->getAccessID();
} else {
    header('Location: ' . $config['auth']['login_url'] . $config['general']['url_root']);
    exit;
}
```

If your app looks like that, read on. Other Wayne Auth shapes need a hand move to `sesame_login()` (see [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)):

- An app that reads the `validUser` cookie itself and posts it to a cookie validator, or to the Wayne Auth HTTP gateway.
- An app that asks Wayne Auth for the user's **password** (`_parseSSOCookie('d')`, or a client built with `'d'`). CAS never gives an app the password, so no bridge can; that app needs a different design (a service account, or the target system's own SSO).

SESAME needs PHP 8.3 or newer. An app on older PHP moves its PHP first ([Booster](https://github.com/waynestate/booster) does that part).

### The one-line swap[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#the-one-line-swap)

1. Require SESAME with Composer (`composer require waynestate/sesame guzzlehttp/guzzle`). Guzzle is the HTTP client the cas driver uses to check tickets; any PSR-18 client works if you pass it yourself.
2. Add the app's SESAME config file, for example `config/sesame.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Waynestate\Sesame\WayneAuth\WayneAuth;

require_once __DIR__ . '/../vendor/autoload.php';

WayneAuth::boot([
    'driver' => 'cas',
    'environment' => 'production',
    'cas' => [
        'base_url' => 'https://login.wayne.edu/cas',
        'service_url' => 'https://app.apps.wayne.edu/',
    ],
]);
```

3. Change the one line that loaded the old class:

```php
// Before
require_once('lib/WayneAuth/WayneAuth.php');

// After
require_once('config/sesame.php');
```

That is the whole code change. `boot()` builds SESAME, registers it with `sesame()`, and makes the old global name `WayneAuth` point at the bridge, so every `new WayneAuth($config['wayneauth'])` in the app gets the bridge. An app that refers to the class by a `use` line can import `Waynestate\Sesame\WayneAuth\WayneAuth` instead. Delete the old class file once nothing loads it: `boot()` refuses to start while a different `WayneAuth` class is loaded, so a half-done swap fails loudly instead of quietly keeping Wayne Auth.

The `cas.service_url` is where CAS sends people back: the page that calls `authenticateSSO()` (or one that every page passes through). After the sign-in, people land there, the way Wayne Auth's `forward_url` sent them to the app's root. With [Playbook](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.html) installed, or `SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL` set, `base_url` can be left out.

#### The session[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#the-session)

The app owns the session, as everywhere in SESAME: call `session_start()` before the first `authenticateSSO()`. Wayne Auth needed no session because the SSO cookie was the session; CAS needs one to remember who signed in. Most Wayne Auth apps already start one. Let HELMET harden it if you can ([Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html) has the cookie settings), and set `session.gc_maxlifetime` to at least the idle timeout.

Legacy apps usually start the session before Composer's autoloader is loaded. That is fine: `boot()` re-reads SESAME's values in the session once the autoloader is there, so nobody looks signed out.

#### Options[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#options)

`boot()` takes a few more arguments, all optional:

| Argument | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$http` | Guzzle, 10 second timeout, redirects off | The PSR-18 client for the ticket check |
| `$requests` | nyholm/psr7's factory | The PSR-17 request factory |
| `$resolver` | the verified username | Your `UserResolver`, when the app wants its own user object stored in the session |
| `$options['on_guest']` | `redirect` | `redirect` sends a visitor who is not signed in to CAS from inside `authenticateSSO()`; `deny` answers `false` the way Wayne Auth did, so the app's own else branch runs |
| `$options['accessid_case']` | `asis` | `upper` or `lower` when the app compares the AccessID against a list written in one case |
| `$logger` | none | A PSR-3 logger for SESAME's sign-in events |

With `on_guest` left at `redirect`, the app's old else branch (the redirect to the Wayne Auth login page) never runs again, so the old login URL in its config stops mattering. With `deny`, point that login URL at a page of your own that calls `sesame_login()`.

### What changes, call by call[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#what-changes-call-by-call)

| Wayne Auth | The bridge |
| --- | --- |
| `new WayneAuth($config)` | Same. The old keys (`sso_host`, `sso_port`, `ldap_host`, `timeout` and the rest) are accepted and ignored; `$wayne_auth->config` still holds them |
| `authenticateSSO()` true | Same: someone is signed in. SESAME's idle (120 minutes) and absolute (12 hours) timeouts apply |
| `authenticateSSO()` false for a visitor with no cookie | Sends the visitor to CAS and stops the script (`on_guest => redirect`), or `false` (`on_guest => deny`) |
| (nothing) | A visitor coming back from CAS with a ticket: the ticket is checked, the user is stored, and the browser is sent on to the service URL without the ticket |
| (nothing) | A ticket that does not check out throws `AuthenticationFailed`. Answering `false` would send the browser to CAS and back forever |
| `false` for a refused visitor | Your resolver returned `null`: `false`, nothing stored |
| `getAccessID()` | The CAS username, the same AccessID. `$wayne_auth->accessid` is set too |
| `_parseSSOCookie('v')` | `['verified' => true, 'accessid' => ..., 'timeout' => seconds left]`, or `['verified' => false]`; never redirects |
| `_parseSSOCookie('d')` (the password) | Throws `LogicException`. CAS never gives an app the password |
| Signing out through the SSO logout page | A POST form to a page that calls `sesame_logout()` ([Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html#logout)); it ends the app's session and sends the browser to the CAS logout |

Wayne Auth told an app the AccessID and nothing else, so nothing an app read from it is lost. CAS can release more (name, email, groups) as attributes: those arrive in the `Identity` your resolver receives, once you move to the native calls.

### Check it before you ship[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#check-it-before-you-ship)

1. On a laptop, boot with the `fake` driver (`'driver' => 'fake', 'environment' => 'local', 'fake' => ['username' => 'ab1234']]`): every page should say who is signed in without any CAS server.
2. On pre-production, with the real `cas` config: open a page in a private window. You should land on the CAS sign-in, come back to the service URL with no `ticket` in the address bar, and see the app signed in as you. Check the AccessID's case against any `authorized_ids` list the app keeps.
3. Leave the tab alone past the idle timeout and reload: you should go through CAS again (silently, if your CAS session is still alive).
4. Grep the app for `validUser`, `sso_host` and `_parseSSOCookie('d')`: none should be left doing work.

SESAME's own tests do the same end to end: a fixture page written the Wayne Auth way signs in through the bridge under PHP's built-in server, with a fake CAS answer (`tests/WayneAuthLegacyAppTest.php`).

### Going native later[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#going-native-later)

The bridge is three thin calls over SESAME's raw-PHP functions. When you have a quiet afternoon:

| Bridge | Native |
| --- | --- |
| `require_once('config/sesame.php')` with `WayneAuth::boot()` | the same file, building `Sesame` as in [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html) and calling `sesame($sesame)` |
| `if ($wayne_auth->authenticateSSO()) { ... } else { redirect }` | `$user = sesame_login();` (it sends guests to CAS and stops the script) |
| `$wayne_auth->getAccessID()` | the username your `UserResolver` received, or `sesame()->sessionStatus()['username']` |
| `authorized_ids` checks after the sign-in | your resolver returns `null` for anyone not allowed, so they are never signed in |

Then delete the config line that calls `boot()`, and the bridge is gone.

### Related[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-off-wayne-auth.html#related)

- [Raw PHP](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/raw-php.html)
- [The cas driver](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/driver-cas.html)
- [Moving from wayne-cas](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html)
- [Session timeouts](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session-timeouts.html)
