## Decision: the 60 second regenerate grace[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/regenerate-grace.html#decision-the-60-second-regenerate-grace)

When SESAME regenerates the session ID at login, it does not delete the old session at once. It keeps the old session for a short grace, so a user on a slow network does not lose the login, and a reuse after the grace is treated as a possible hijack.

### Decision[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/regenerate-grace.html#decision)

`NativeSession::regenerate()` marks the old session with a "destroyed at" time and the new ID, keeps it for a 60 second grace, and copies the data to the new session. The constructor takes `graceSeconds`, and 60 is the default.

### Why[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/regenerate-grace.html#why)

The [PHP manual](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.session-regenerate-id.php) says `session_regenerate_id()` does not handle an unstable network well. When the old ID is deleted at once, a user whose browser is still sending the old ID can lose the session when the response with the new ID never arrives. Deleting at once also removes the chance to see a stolen ID being replayed. The manual's example keeps the old session for 300 seconds; that is the example's choice, not a rule. The full reasoning is in `BEST_PRACTICES.md`, section S43.

### Turning it off[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/regenerate-grace.html#turning-it-off)

Pass `graceSeconds: 0` to the `NativeSession` constructor to restore the immediate delete. A negative value is refused with an `InvalidArgumentException`.

### After the grace[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/regenerate-grace.html#after-the-grace)

A use of the old ID after the grace is treated as a possible hijack: the session is retired, a clean one starts, and `sesame.session_anomaly` is logged as a warning with `reason` `destroyed_session_reused` when a logger is set. The log carries no session ID or session data.

### Not covered[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/regenerate-grace.html#not-covered)

The Laravel adapter uses the framework's own regenerate and is unchanged. Logout is a separate path: `invalidate()` retires the session, leaving a short-lived logout marker in the store by default (S7).

### Tests[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/regenerate-grace.html#tests)

`NativeSessionTest` covers the behavior:

- `testRegenerateKeepsTheOldSessionDuringTheGrace`
- `testTheOldSessionIsStillUsableWithinTheGrace`
- `testTheOldSessionIsRejectedAfterTheGraceAndLogged`
- `testZeroGraceDeletesTheOldSessionAtOnce`
- `testANegativeGraceIsRefused`
- `testTheAnomalyLogCarriesNoSessionIdOrData`

---

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html

## The saml driver's library choice[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html#the-saml-driver-s-library-choice)

Ali Baba did not forge his own cave door, and SESAME does not write its own XML signature checks. This note records which library the `saml` driver stands on, what else was weighed, and why. Data checked on 2026-11-07 against Packagist (`repo.packagist.org/p2/<package>.json`) and the Packagist security advisory API.

### What the driver needs[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html#what-the-driver-needs)

- A service provider for the Web Browser SSO profile: an AuthnRequest over the HTTP-Redirect binding (optionally signed), the Response over HTTP-POST.
- Response validation in one place: the XML schema, XML signature verification that also checks what the signature covers (the classic wrapping attacks), Destination, Recipient, Audience, Issuer, InResponseTo, the time conditions and the bearer subject confirmation.
- IdP metadata parsing and SP metadata generation.
- A small dependency tree, a permissive license (SESAME is MIT), PHP 8.3 to 8.5, and an active maintainer with a record of fixing advisories.

### The candidates[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html#the-candidates)

| Package | Latest release | License | PHP | Dependencies | Advisories (all time) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onelogin/php-saml | 4.4.1, 2026-11-04 (4.3.2, 2026-05-07, on the 4.3 line) | MIT | >=8.0 (4.4), >=7.3 (4.3) | robrichards/xmlseclibs only (4.4 pulls xmlseclibs 4, which brings phpseclib 3; 4.3 uses xmlseclibs 3.1, with no further packages) | 3, the newest (CVE-2025-66475, through xmlseclibs) fixed in 4.3.1 |
| simplesamlphp/saml2 | v6.3.1, 2026-11-05; v7 in release candidates | LGPL-2.1-or-later | ^8.2 to ^8.5 by release; v7 needs ^8.5 | nyholm/psr7, psr/clock, psr/log, simplesamlphp/assert, xml-common, xml-security and xml-soap | 9, two of them in July 2026 (CVE-2026-49283, CVE-2026-49289); simplesamlphp/xml-security has 2 more |

### The choice: onelogin/php-saml[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html#the-choice-onelogin-php-saml)

- **One library, one reading.** php-saml's `Response::isValid()` does every check in the list above in strict mode, against the one parsed document it verified, and reads the assertion through the reference its signature points at. SESAME reads its extra values (IssueInstant, AuthnInstant, the class reference) through the same document and the same query (S47).
- **The smaller surface.** One dependency (xmlseclibs), against seven packages for simplesamlphp/saml2, most of them its own XML stack.
- **The license.** MIT, like SESAME. simplesamlphp/saml2 is LGPL, which is usable but is one more thing every app has to think about.
- **The record.** Three advisories in its life, each fixed promptly; the last, through xmlseclibs, was fixed in 4.3.1 the day it was published. simplesamlphp/saml2's newer releases also move their PHP floor around (v6.3.0 and v6.2.2 to v6.2.4 required PHP 8.5; v6.3.1 dropped it again), which would make SESAME's own PHP support follow theirs.

simplesamlphp/saml2 is the strongest alternative if SESAME ever needs the whole SAML protocol (artifact binding, SOAP, attribute queries); the driver needs only Web Browser SSO.

### The floor (SESAME-22)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html#the-floor-sesame-22)

SESAME refuses php-saml below **4.3.2** and xmlseclibs below **3.1.5**:

- php-saml 4.3.1 fixed CVE-2025-66475 (signature verification through xmlseclibs), and 4.3.2 requires xmlseclibs 3.1.5 or later.
- xmlseclibs 3.1.4 fixed CVE-2025-66578 (a canonicalization error) and 3.1.5 fixed CVE-2026-32313 (a missing AES-GCM tag check on encrypted data).

The floor is held three ways, so it cannot drift:

1. `composer.json` lists both under `conflict`, so Composer refuses to install an older release beside SESAME.
2. `SamlDriver::assertLibraryInstalled()` checks the installed versions through Composer's runtime API when the driver is built, and refuses a dev branch, because nothing says it holds the fixes.
3. `tests/SamlConfigTest.php` fails when the installed versions are below the floor, or when `composer.json` and the driver's constants disagree.

`^4.3.2` takes either line. On 4.3 the tree is php-saml and xmlseclibs 3.1; on 4.4 (what the lock file has today) xmlseclibs 4 adds phpseclib 3 and two small paragonie packages. The driver's tests pass on both. `composer audit` in CI covers phpseclib's own advisories.

### How the dependency is kept optional[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html#how-the-dependency-is-kept-optional)

onelogin/php-saml is in `suggest` and `require-dev`, not `require`, the same way SESAME treats league/oauth2-client. Only the `saml` driver needs it. When it is missing, building the driver fails with:

```
The saml driver needs onelogin/php-saml. Install it with: composer require onelogin/php-saml
```

### What SESAME adds on top[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/saml-library-choice.html#what-sesame-adds-on-top)

php-saml is configured strictly (`strict`, `wantAssertionsSigned`, `wantXMLValidation`, `requireDestination`, `destinationStrictlyMatches`, `rejectUnsolicitedResponsesWithInResponseTo`, and no RequestedAuthnContext unless the app asks for one). SESAME then adds what php-saml leaves to the app:

- **The two-hop ACS.** The IdP's cross-site POST carries no Lax session cookie, so the ACS parks the Response under a single-use handle and the check runs on the following GET, where the session is back (S35).
- **The pending request in the session**, so a Response is accepted only for a sign-in this browser started (login CSRF), and only once.
- **The replay guard**, keyed on the issuer and the assertion ID.
- **SHA-2 only.** php-saml still verifies SHA-1 signatures; SESAME refuses them.
- **Its own clock.** php-saml checks the conditions against the system clock with a fixed 180-second drift. SESAME also checks the IssueInstant against the injected PSR-20 clock, with its own leeway and maximum age.
- **The ACS URL, not the request.** php-saml compares Destination and Recipient with "the current URL" from `$_SERVER`. SESAME runs the check as if the request were at the configured ACS URL (`AcsUrl::during()`), which is also right behind a TLS-terminating proxy.
- **RelayState through ReturnTo**, checked on the way out and again on the way back.

---

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html

## Troubleshooting[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

Open sesame opens the door; this page is for when it does not. Each symptom below names the cause the sources give, the fix, and a check you can run. If your sign-in still fails after these, start at [Quick start](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html) with the `fake` driver to prove the wiring, then come back with the real driver.

### Sign-in fails[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#sign-in-fails)

#### The oidc driver fails to build: `The oidc driver needs league/oauth2-client` [#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-oidc-driver-fails-to-build-the-oidc-driver-needs-league-oauth2-client)

**Cause.** The `oidc` driver stands on `league/oauth2-client`, which SESAME suggests but does not require. Without it, building the driver fails with `The oidc driver needs league/oauth2-client. Install it with: composer require league/oauth2-client`.

**Fix.** Install the library:

```
composer require league/oauth2-client
```

**Check.** Build the driver again; the error is gone and the sign-in starts. The driver's behavior is covered by `tests/OidcDriverTest.php`.

#### The saml driver fails to build: `The saml driver needs onelogin/php-saml` [#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-saml-driver-fails-to-build-the-saml-driver-needs-onelogin-php-saml)

**Cause.** The `saml` driver stands on `onelogin/php-saml`, which SESAME suggests but does not require, and it refuses php-saml older than 4.3.2 or xmlseclibs older than 3.1.5 (both had signature or encryption advisories).

**Fix.** Install or update the library:

```
composer require onelogin/php-saml
composer update onelogin/php-saml robrichards/xmlseclibs
```

**Check.** Build the driver again; the error is gone. The floor is covered by `tests/SamlConfigTest.php`.

#### A SAML sign-in fails with `saml.handle` or `saml.in_response_to` [#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-saml-sign-in-fails-with-saml-handle-or-saml-in-response-to)

**Cause.** The finish could not find what the start and the ACS left behind. `saml.handle`: the parked response is gone (more than two minutes, used twice, or a cache the web servers do not share). `saml.in_response_to`: the session that started the sign-in is not the one finishing it (a different browser, a session cookie set to `SameSite=Strict`, a session started on the ACS page, or a sign-in older than ten minutes).

**Fix.** Use a cache store every web server shares (`SESAME_SAML_CACHE_STORE`), keep the session cookie `SameSite=Lax`, and never start the session on the ACS page (raw PHP) or put the ACS route in the `web` group (Laravel).

**Check.** A fresh sign-in from the app's login URL completes. The flow is covered by `tests/SamlDriverTest.php` and `tests/Laravel/SamlRouteTest.php`.

#### A `cas` login loops back to the CAS login page[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-cas-login-loops-back-to-the-cas-login-page)

**Cause.** `cas.renew` is set to `true` against Academica. Academica does not issue a ticket for `renew=true` and sends the user back to the login page, so a `renew` login loops instead of signing in.

**Fix.** Leave `cas.renew` off (the default is `false`). Set it to `true` only when the app needs a fresh, direct login rather than an existing SSO session, and the CAS server issues tickets for it.

**Check.** Sign in with the default `cas.renew`; the ticket completes and the user lands on the service URL. `tests/CasDriverTest.php` covers the cas sign-in steps.

#### CAS validation redirects to the login page, or attributes are missing[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#cas-validation-redirects-to-the-login-page-or-attributes-are-missing)

**Cause.** `cas.protocol` is `3.0` against Academica, which is believed to redirect cookieless `/p3/serviceValidate` calls to the login page. Protocol `2.0` is the default for that reason.

**Fix.** Keep `cas.protocol` at `2.0`. Set it to `3.0` only when a CAS server releases attributes on `/p3/serviceValidate`.

**Check.** Validate a ticket with `cas.protocol` at `2.0`; the identity comes back with its attributes. `tests/CasDriverTest.php` covers it.

#### A sign-in fails on a hung or slow CAS server, or a client that is set up wrong[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-sign-in-fails-on-a-hung-or-slow-cas-server-or-a-client-that-is-set-up-wrong)

**Cause.** SESAME treats any non-200 answer (including a redirect) as a failed login and lets a client exception through, so a PSR-18 client that is set up wrong fails the sign-in and never signs anyone in. Guzzle has no total timeout by default, so a hung CAS server would hold the request open forever, and it follows up to five redirects by default, to any host or to plain http.

**Fix.** Hand SESAME a client with a timeout, redirects off for the validation call, and TLS verification on:

```php
$http = new \GuzzleHttp\Client([
    'timeout' => 10,
    'connect_timeout' => 5,
    'allow_redirects' => false,
    'verify' => true,
]);
```

**Check.** Run the suite; the fail-closed behavior on a redirect and on a client exception is proven by tests (S42):

docker

```bash
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

local

```bash
vendor/bin/phpunit
```

#### A failed login shows the CAS failure code to the user[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-failed-login-shows-the-cas-failure-code-to-the-user)

**Cause.** An `AuthenticationFailed` message can carry the CAS failure code (for example `INVALID_TICKET`), which tells an attacker how the server refused the ticket.

**Fix.** Log the message for operators and show the user one generic line instead.

**Check.** Trigger a failed login with a bad ticket; the log carries the message and the page shows the generic line. `tests/CasDriverTest.php` covers the failure path.

#### The gateway driver refuses every assertion from an untrusted peer[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-gateway-driver-refuses-every-assertion-from-an-untrusted-peer)

**Cause.** The request must come from a trusted proxy: the direct peer (`REMOTE_ADDR`) must match one of the configured CIDR ranges in `gateway.trusted_proxies`. A valid assertion from an untrusted peer is still rejected, and a plain identity header (`Remote-User`, `X-Remote-User`, or any spelling of them) is never read.

**Fix.** List the CIDR ranges (or single IPs) the gateway proxy sits behind in `gateway.trusted_proxies`, a non-empty array.

**Check.** Send a request through the gateway proxy; the assertion verifies and the user signs in. `tests/GatewayDriverTest.php` covers the trust checks.

#### The gateway driver throws `InvalidConfig` naming a key at boot[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-gateway-driver-throws-invalidconfig-naming-a-key-at-boot)

**Cause.** With the gateway driver, `DriverFactory::make()` throws `InvalidConfig` naming the key when `gateway.public_key`, `gateway.issuer` or `gateway.audience` is null or empty, instead of passing an empty string into the driver.

**Fix.** Set the named key. All three are required for the gateway driver, along with a non-empty `gateway.trusted_proxies`.

**Check.** Boot the driver; it builds without `InvalidConfig`.

#### A truthy `slo` (or `single_logout`) config key is rejected at boot[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-truthy-slo-or-single-logout-config-key-is-rejected-at-boot)

**Cause.** Single logout is not supported: the identity provider cannot sign the user out of the app's other sessions, so SESAME rejects a truthy `slo` (or `single_logout`) config key with `InvalidConfig` at boot, a mistake to fail on early rather than at the first logout.

**Fix.** Remove the `slo` (or `single_logout`) key from the config.

**Check.** Boot the app; it starts, and a logout clears the app session and sends `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Clear-Site-Data: "cache", "storage"`.

#### The `fake` driver refuses to boot in production[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-fake-driver-refuses-to-boot-in-production)

**Cause.** The `fake` driver is for local development and tests only; it refuses to boot in production.

**Fix.** Use a real driver in production: `cas` for a Citadel app today, `gateway` once Drawbridge is live, or `oidc` or `oauth2` for apps off Citadel. See [Which driver for my app?](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/which-driver.html).

**Check.** In the local environment the `fake` driver signs in; in production the configured driver does. `tests/FakeDriverTest.php` covers the refusal.

### The session ends too soon, or looks wrong[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-session-ends-too-soon-or-looks-wrong)

#### A raw-PHP app signs people out after 24 quiet minutes[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-raw-php-app-signs-people-out-after-24-quiet-minutes)

**Cause.** PHP's default `session.gc_maxlifetime` is 1440 seconds (24 minutes), and PHP's garbage collector deletes session data older than that, so on the defaults a raw-PHP app signs people out after 24 quiet minutes, long before SESAME's 120-minute idle timeout. SESAME never starts the session, so it cannot change this for you.

**Fix.** Set `session.gc_maxlifetime = 7200` (your `session.idle_minutes` times 60) in `php.ini` or the FPM pool, or call `ini_set('session.gc_maxlifetime', '7200')` before `session_start()`. Laravel apps set `SESSION_LIFETIME` (minutes) instead.

**Check.** The exact call the sources use, in the oidc raw-PHP example:

```php
ini_set('session.gc_maxlifetime', '7200'); // at least SESAME's idle timeout; see Raw PHP
```

Then sit a signed-in session for more than 24 quiet minutes; it stays signed in until the idle timeout (120 minutes by default) drops it.

#### The log carries a `sesame.session_anomaly` warning[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-log-carries-a-sesame-session-anomaly-warning)

**Cause.** The session state looks wrong or tampered with: `reason` is `missing_timestamps` (a user stored without the session's timestamps; the session is signed out right after, so the anomaly precedes the `sesame.logout`) or `bad_session_ref` (a stored `sesame.session_ref` that is not a 16-character lowercase hex string; the user stays signed in and the bad value is never echoed into the log). A session without a reference at all is not an anomaly.

**Fix.** Look at the `session_ref` and the user around it in the log to see what happened to the session. `sesame.login` and `sesame.logout` also carry `session_ref`, the opaque 16-character hex reference that ties the login, timeouts and logout of one sign-in together in the log.

**Check.** Grep the log for `sesame.session_anomaly` and follow the `session_ref` value across the events of that sign-in. `tests/SesameEventsTest.php` covers the events.

#### The session is missing on the return from the identity provider[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-session-is-missing-on-the-return-from-the-identity-provider)

**Cause.** The session cookie is `SameSite=Strict`. The identity provider sends the browser back to the app with a cross-site top-level `GET`, and a `Strict` cookie is not sent on that request: it would be missing, so the app would see no session on the return request and any login binding would fail for every user.

**Fix.** Keep the cookie `SameSite=Lax`, never `Strict`. In raw PHP HELMET makes both choices for you (`SessionHardening::apply()`, called by `helmet_boot()`); in Laravel the default is `Lax`, and the settings are `SESSION_COOKIE=__Host-wsu-session`, `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true`, `SESSION_PATH=/` with `SESSION_DOMAIN` empty in `config/session.php`.

**Check.** Sign in end to end; the return request carries the cookie and the login completes. A cross-site `POST` carries no `Lax` cookie at all, which is the defense you want.

#### A stale session is signed out on the spot[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-stale-session-is-signed-out-on-the-spot)

**Cause.** Every signed-in session has two clocks: the idle timeout (default `session.idle_minutes` `120`) and the absolute lifetime (default `session.absolute_minutes` `720`). Both are checked on every `user()` call, so a stale session is signed out the first time anything asks who is signed in. A session made before the timeouts existed (a user, no timestamps) counts as expired.

**Fix.** This is the expected behavior, not a fault. If the limits are wrong for the app, set `session.idle_minutes` and `session.absolute_minutes` (env `SESAME_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES` and `SESAME_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MINUTES` in Laravel). See [Session timeouts](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session-timeouts.html).

**Check.** Read the user with `sesame_user()` after the quiet time; the session is gone and the next `sesame_login()` starts fresh.

### Config and playbook[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#config-and-playbook)

#### Boot fails: `Missing required setting SESAME_....` [#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#boot-fails-missing-required-setting-sesame)

**Cause.** The setting is not in the environment and the private `waynestate/playbook` package, which supplies the university's values when the environment is empty, is not installed. A missing routed setting fails with `Missing required setting SESAME_.... Set it in the environment, or install waynestate/playbook (see the README).`

**Fix.** Set the variable in the environment, as with every other setting, or install the playbook:

```json
{
    "repositories": [
        { "type": "vcs", "url": "https://git.wayne.edu/enterprise-apps/playbook.git" }
    ]
}
```

```
composer require waynestate/playbook
```

The environment always wins: a set variable beats the playbook, and an empty one counts as unset.

**Check.** Boot the app with the environment empty; it reads the four shared values from the playbook and starts. `tests/SettingTest.php` covers the resolution order.

#### Fetching the playbook answers 404[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#fetching-the-playbook-answers-404)

**Cause.** Playbook is private on git.wayne.edu.

**Fix.** Ask the Enterprise Applications team for read access. The token is your own: `read_api` for curl, `read_repository` for clone and Composer.

**Check.** Refetch; the file arrives as plain `KEY=value` lines. Copy the ones you need into your app's `.env` (or your Citadel environment); SESAME does not read `.env.playbook` itself.

linux

```bash
curl --fail -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_TOKEN" "https://git.wayne.edu/api/v4/projects/enterprise-apps%2Fplaybook/repository/files/playbook.env/raw?ref=main" -o .env.playbook
```

windows

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Headers @{ 'PRIVATE-TOKEN' = $env:GITLAB_TOKEN } -Uri "https://git.wayne.edu/api/v4/projects/enterprise-apps%2Fplaybook/repository/files/playbook.env/raw?ref=main" -OutFile .env.playbook
```

Warning

The token in those commands is a secret. Keep it in the environment, never in the repository, and remember Composer keeps the git.wayne.edu credentials it asks for in `auth.json` as an `http-basic` entry.

#### The app still reads wayne-cas names and you expect SESAME behavior[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-app-still-reads-wayne-cas-names-and-you-expect-sesame-behavior)

**Cause.** The app moved to SESAME through the shim, which keeps the wayne-cas names and behavior and says once (in the log) that it is a deprecated bridge. For example, `use2FA` runs a Duo challenge the shim does not carry: when the app still has `wayne-cas.use2FA` switched on, the shim logs a warning once and leaves the 2FA to the app.

**Fix.** Follow the mapping in [Moving from wayne-cas](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/moving-from-wayne-cas.html), or take the easy way: Booster's `cas-to-sesame` hop, planned with `--sesame`.

**Check.** After the move, log in through the pre-production host before you ship, and check the session timeout, the Access ID attribute and Duo there. `tests/Laravel/WayneCasShimTest.php` covers the shim.

### Build, CI and docs[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#build-ci-and-docs)

#### `composer ci` fails[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-ci-fails)

**Cause.** `composer ci` runs the whole gate: validate through tests, Pint and PHPStan, plus the agent-ready and docs checks and the locked-dependency audit. The same command runs on GitLab and GitHub, and both pipelines run the same five checks (manifest, tests, Pint, PHPStan, audit), so a green build means the same thing on both sides.

**Fix.** Read the failing step; static analysis is PHPStan at level 8 from Pinstripe's strict preset, where a call to a deprecated method fails the build.

**Check.** Rerun the gate locally:

docker

```bash
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

local

```bash
composer ci
```

#### `composer docs:check` fails in CI[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-docs-check-fails-in-ci)

**Cause.** The built docs site is stale, or the generated environment reference has drifted from the source.

**Fix.** Rebuild the docs site:

```
composer docs
```

**Check.** `composer docs:check` passes again, and the rebuilt pages under `site/docs/` match what you committed.

#### No PHP on the machine, and the suite will not run[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#no-php-on-the-machine-and-the-suite-will-not-run)

**Cause.** The developer machine has no PHP, so `vendor/bin/phpunit` cannot start.

**Fix.** Docker runs the suite:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -v stack-composer-cache:/tmp/cache -w /app composer:2 composer install --no-interaction
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.3-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app php:8.5-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

**Check.** All three PHP versions pass. How to build, test and release this project is in MAINTAINING.md.

- [Upgrading](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html): what changed between the versions.

---

Source: https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html

## Upgrading[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

How to move between SESAME versions. Each section below is one released version from the changelog that carries a break; sections without a break say so in one sentence and give the upgrade command. Start at the version you are on, work down toward the one you want, and run the checks after each hop.

### 0.6.1 (2026-11-08)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-6-1-2026-11-08)

No breaks. SESAME's routes now point at `SesameController` methods instead of closures, with the same names, URIs and middleware, so `php artisan route:cache` and `php artisan optimize` work in an app that uses SESAME. A Citadel release runs `optimize`, so an app that turned it off for SESAME (Squire's `SQUIRE_ARTISAN_OPTIMIZE=0`) can turn it back on.

**Steps.** `composer update waynestate/sesame` (the `^0.6` constraint already allows 0.6.1).

**How to verify.** `php artisan route:cache` exits 0, `php artisan route:list --name=sesame` lists the routes as `SesameController` actions, and sign-in and sign-out work as before. Then `php artisan route:clear` if you cache routes only at release time.

### 0.6.0 (2026-11-08)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-6-0-2026-11-08)

**Breaking.** Nothing for an app that keeps its driver: the `saml` driver, OAuth2 token introspection and the logged-out session marker are additions, each off until it is configured. One install-time catch: `composer.json` now conflicts with `onelogin/php-saml` below 4.3.2 and `robrichards/xmlseclibs` below 3.1.5 (SESAME-22), so an app that already has an older copy of either cannot take 0.6 until it updates them.

**Deprecated.** Nothing is deprecated in this release.

**Steps.**

1. Update the package (and, if Composer reports the conflict above, the SAML libraries with it):
   ```
   composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.6
   ```
2. Optional: turn on what is new. The `saml` driver is in the README driver table; introspection for opaque OAuth2 tokens is `oauth2.introspection_url` (env `SESAME_OAUTH2_INTROSPECTION_URL`).

**How to verify.** Sign in and out once with the driver the app uses; both work as before.

### 0.5.0 (2026-11-07)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-5-0-2026-11-07)

**Breaking.** The `cas` driver now binds each sign-in to the browser that started it: before the redirect to CAS it stores a pending-login marker in the app's session, and a returning ticket is accepted only against a live marker (single use, ten minutes). A ticket with no live marker is refused before any HTTP call to the CAS server, which blocks login CSRF. Two consequences for apps on the `cas` driver:

1. Apps that build the driver by hand must pass the app's `SessionPort` as the seventh argument to `DriverFactory::make()`; without it the driver refuses to start with `InvalidConfig` unless the binding is switched off. The Laravel adapter passes the app's session itself, so Laravel apps need no code change.
2. An app that accepts a ticket for a login it did not start (a link from the CAS login page) must set `cas.require_pending_login` (env `SESAME_CAS_REQUIRE_PENDING_LOGIN`) to `false`; that reopens login CSRF, so keep the opt-out deliberate.

**Deprecated.** Nothing is deprecated in this release.

**Added.** `gateway.jwks_file` (env `SESAME_GATEWAY_JWKS_FILE`) reads the gateway's public keys from the JWKS file Drawbridge publishes. Nothing changes for an app that keeps `gateway.public_key`. An app on a one-entry `gateway.public_keys` map now also accepts an assertion with no `kid`.

**Changed.** On Laravel 13, implement `RefreshesUser` in the app's resolver: Laravel 13 stores sessions as JSON, so the stored user comes back as an array, and the method must look the user up again; see [Reading the user](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/laravel.html#reading-the-user).

**Steps.**

1. Move the constraint and update:
   ```
   composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.5
   ```
2. If the app builds the `cas` driver by hand (raw PHP), pass the app's session as the seventh argument to `DriverFactory::make()`:
   ```php
   $driver = DriverFactory::make($config, $http, new Psr17Factory(), null, null, null, new NativeSession());
   ```
3. Only if the app must accept a ticket for a login it did not start (a link from the CAS login page), set `cas.require_pending_login` to `false` (env `SESAME_CAS_REQUIRE_PENDING_LOGIN`).

**How to verify.** Sign in through CAS the normal way (the app sends the browser to CAS, the browser returns with the ticket); the sign-in succeeds and the marker is spent. Then deliver a just-issued ticket from a browser profile that never started a sign-in: it is refused with `This sign-in was not started in this browser, or it took too long. Start again from the app.`, and no HTTP call reaches the CAS server. `tests/CasDriverTest.php` covers all of it under the frozen names `testLoginBinding*`.

### 0.4.0 (2026-11-03)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-4-0-2026-11-03)

**Breaking.** The `gateway` driver now refuses a token whose `typ` header is `at+jwt` or `application/at+jwt`, so an OAuth2 access token cannot be replayed as a gateway assertion. A missing `typ` or `JWT` still works. This is a pre-1.0 minor: apps that pin `^0.3` stay on 0.3.x until they move their constraint to `^0.4`.

**Deprecated.** Nothing is deprecated in this release.

**Steps.**

1. Move the constraint and update:
   ```
   composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.4
   ```
2. If your app sends OAuth2 access tokens to a gateway endpoint, stop: those tokens are refused now by design. Route API calls through the `oauth2` driver instead.
3. Optional new pieces you can adopt now: `session_ref`, a per sign-in correlation id that ties the auth events of one sign-in together in the log; `Identity::isFromNewLogin()` and `Identity::usedLongTermToken()` for CAS; optional PSR-3 logging of authentication events (`sesame.log`, env `SESAME_LOG`, default `true`); `oauth2.require_at_jwt` (env `SESAME_OAUTH2_REQUIRE_AT_JWT`), off by default because Microsoft Entra v2 access tokens are typed `JWT`; and `gateway.public_keys`, a map of `kid` to public key for key rotation without a coordinated window.

**How to verify.** Run the gate:

```
composer ci
```

then sign in through the gateway with a normal assertion (missing `typ` or `JWT`) and confirm a replayed `at+jwt` token is refused.

### 0.3.0 (2026-10-30)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-3-0-2026-10-30)

**Breaking.** The signed-in user is looked up again on every request when the app's resolver implements the new `RefreshesUser` interface, and a user who no longer exists signs the session out. Before, `Sesame::user()` returned the copy saved at sign-in, so a user whose role was removed kept it until the session ended. The wayne-cas `UserResolver` implements it (a plain find by primary key, never an import). Also fixed in this release: the wayne-cas `WayneAuthenticate` middleware used to send `/login` to itself forever, and resolving SESAME used to build the driver, which broke guests on http, artisan commands, queue workers and tests.

**Deprecated.** Nothing is deprecated in this release.

**Steps.**

1. Update the package:
   ```
   composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.3
   ```
2. If the app reads the user through `auth()->user()`, point the guard at the new `sesame` driver: set `auth.guards.web.driver` to `sesame` and the users provider to `eloquent`. A Laravel login, `onceUsingId()` or `actingAs()` still wins for the request.
3. Check the user model: it needs the exact method `public function getReadOnlyAttributes($persistedAttributes = []): array` (public, with the parameter), since the wayne-cas `WayneCasable` interface and `ReadOnlyAttributes` trait now agree on one signature.

**How to verify.** Sign in, then remove a user's role (or the account) while the session is live; the next request reflects the change, and a deleted user is signed out. `tests/Laravel/SesameGuardTest.php` and `tests/Laravel/ReadOnlyAttributesTest.php` cover the guard and the model shape.

### 0.2.2 (2026-10-29)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-2-2026-10-29)

**Breaking.** The oidc driver's default roles claim is `wsu_roles`, the name Entra sends. Apps that relied on the old default must set `roles_claim` (and `claims`) to `wsuRoles` to keep the old name.

**Deprecated.** Nothing is deprecated in this release.

**Steps.**

1. Update the package:
   ```
   composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.2
   ```
2. If the app reads roles from the oidc identity under the old name, add `oidc.roles_claim` (env `SESAME_OIDC_ROLES_CLAIM`) set to `wsuRoles`, and the same for `oidc.claims` (env `SESAME_OIDC_CLAIMS`).

**How to verify.** Sign in with the `oidc` driver and read `$identity->attributes['wsu_roles']` (or the name you configured); the roles arrive under the claim you named.

### 0.2.1 (2026-10-29)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-1-2026-10-29)

No breaks in this release: it adds the agent-ready site from Squire's kit, fixes the oauth2 peg on the site, writes project names as words except acronyms, fixes stale capability claims, and shows the oidc driver on the site. Upgrade with:

```
composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.2
```

### 0.2.0 (2026-10-29)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-2-0-2026-10-29)

**Breaking.** Raw PHP: `sesame_logout()` is POST-only with a CSRF token. It runs only when the POST body's `sesame_logout_token` matches the session's token (new `sesame_logout_token()`, `Sesame::logoutToken()` and `Sesame::isLogoutToken()`); a GET answers 405 and a bad token 403, and neither touches the session. Apps must change a logout link to a POST form carrying the token. The Laravel `POST /logout` route stays in the `web` group and so under Laravel's CSRF check. Also changed: `ReturnTo` (every driver's login and logout return-to) now requires the service URL's scheme, host and effective port, and refuses a URL with a user name or password; before, the host alone was compared, so `https://app.example.test:8443/` passed for a service on 443. Plain http is accepted only for a localhost or 127.0.0.1 service URL. And `DriverFactory::make()` takes the app session as an optional seventh argument (the oidc driver needs it).

**Deprecated.** Nothing is deprecated in this release.

**Steps.**

1. Update the package:
   ```
   composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.2
   ```
2. In raw-PHP apps, replace the logout link with a POST form:
   ```php
   <form method="post" action="/logout.php">
     <input type="hidden" name="sesame_logout_token" value="<?= sesame_logout_token() ?>">
     <button>Sign out</button>
   </form>
   ```
3. If the app passes return-to addresses, make sure they match the service URL's scheme, host and port, and carry no user name or password.
4. If you use the new `oidc` driver, pass the app session as the seventh argument to `DriverFactory::make()`, and install `league/oauth2-client`.

**How to verify.** A GET to the logout endpoint answers 405 and leaves the session alone; a POST without the token answers 403; a POST with the token signs out. `tests/ReturnToTest.php` covers the tightened return-to rule.

### 0.1.3 (2026-10-29)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-3-2026-10-29)

No breaks in this release: the four shared WSU values (`SESAME_CAS_BASE_URL`, `SESAME_GATEWAY_ISSUER`, `SESAME_OAUTH2_ISSUER`, `SESAME_OAUTH2_JWKS_URL`) now resolve through `Waynestate\Sesame\Support\Setting::get()` (the environment wins, and when it is empty the private `waynestate/playbook` package supplies the value, suggested, never required), and a missing routed setting now fails with `Missing required setting SESAME_.... Set it in the environment, or install waynestate/playbook (see the README).` instead of naming the config key. Upgrade with:

```
composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.1
```

### 0.1.2 (2026-10-29)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-2-2026-10-29)

No breaks in this release: the CAS driver reads `serviceValidate` responses by namespace URI instead of prefix, so a body that binds the `cas:` prefix to a different namespace can no longer be read as a success, while a body that binds another prefix (or none) to the real CAS namespace keeps working. Upgrade with:

```
composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.1
```

### 0.1.1 (2026-10-29)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-1-2026-10-29)

**Breaking.** A truthy `slo` (or `single_logout`) config key is now rejected with `InvalidConfig` at boot: the identity provider does not support single logout, so the setting is a mistake to fail on early rather than at the first logout. An app that sets it must remove the key or it will not boot.

**Deprecated.** Nothing is deprecated in this release.

**Steps.**

1. Update the package:
   ```
   composer require waynestate/sesame:^0.1
   ```
2. Remove any `slo` (or `single_logout`) key from the config.
3. New in this release, if you want them: step-up by authentication context (`sesame_require_context(string $id)`, the `sesame.context` Laravel middleware, `Identity::hasAuthContext(string $id)`), `cas.assume_mfa` (default `false`), the `oauth2` driver with its config keys, and `InvalidConfig` naming the key when `gateway.public_key`, `gateway.issuer` or `gateway.audience` is null or empty.

**How to verify.** Boot the app; it starts without `InvalidConfig`, and a context check fails closed when there is no user or no identity. `tests/Laravel/RequireAuthContextTest.php` covers the context check.

### 0.1.0 (2026-10-27)[#](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-0-2026-10-27)

First tagged release. There is nothing to upgrade from. Install with:

```
composer require waynestate/sesame
```
